articles.title: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ LIVE updates | ‘Arnab’ hurtling towards Andhra Pradesh coast
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Several southern Odisha districts started receiving rain as ‘Arnab’ hurtled towards the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 27 2026

Srikakulam district has received widespread rain overnight, as the Severe Cyclonic Storm (SCS) ‘Arnab’ strengthened into a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm (VSCS) at around 11.30 p.m. on Monday (October 26, 2026).

According to latest information from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, the system lay centred at 2.30 a.m. over Westcentral Bay of Bengal, at around 300 km southeast of Vishakhapatnam, 360 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 380 km south of Gopalpur of Odisha, 460 km east of Machilipatnam, 530 km east of Bapatla and 920 km west-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram of the Andaman Islands.
Arnab intensifies to VSCS, showers spread in north Andhra as IMD warns of coastal landfall near Yanam by Oct 28, 2026.
Under the potential impact of cyclone ‘Arnab’, unseasonal rain, thunderstorms and strong winds are likely in Uttar Pradesh between October 28 and 31.

According to the forecast, winds are likely to blow at 30 to 40 kilometres per hour on October 28 in Sonbhadra, Mirzapur, Chandauli, Varanasi, Bhadohi, Ghazipur, and Ballia, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing a yellow alert for these districts.
An orange alert has been issued for October 29 due to the possibility of heavy rainfall and strong winds in several districts.
Rainfall is forecast in several areas, including Chitrakoot, Kaushambi, Prayagraj, Fatehpur, Pratapgarh, Rae Bareli, Amethi and Sultanpur.

On October 30, heavy rain and strong winds are also likely in Bareilly, Pilibhit and Shahjahanpur, along with several districts of Purvanchal, Awadh, and the Terai region. As a result, daytime temperatures may fall by 5 to 8 degrees Celsius.

In light of the forecast, the Uttar Pradesh Relief Commissioner’s Office has issued precautionary guidelines for the general public and farmers, with the administration also laying emphasis on relief and rescue preparations, according to an official statement issued on Monday night.
The Relief Commissioner’s Office has urged people to follow weather-related warnings and the administration’s instructions. -- PTI

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has ordered heightened preparedness across the State in view of the threat posed by Cyclone Arnab, which is expected to bring heavy to extremely heavy rainfall. Roads and Buildings (R&B) Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy has directed officials to ensure road safety and an uninterrupted emergency response.
The cyclone is expected to affect 13 districts with heavy rainfall on October 28 and 29. Wind speeds of 115 to 140 kmph are forecast in 12 districts, according to the State government’s assessments.

articles.title: Jana Sena’s MLC claim sparks unease in Telangana BJP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana BJP president N. Ramachander Rao widely seen as the frontrunner for the Hyderabad-Rangareddy-Mahabubnagar Graduates’ constituency

With Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao widely seen as the frontrunner for the Hyderabad-Rangareddy-Mahabubnagar Graduates’ constituency in the upcoming Legislative Council elections, a request from ally Jana Sena Party (JSP) for the other graduates’ seat has triggered unease within the State BJP leadership.

“The JSP has informally sought BJP support for its nominee, Dr. G. Srinivasa Rao, in the Warangal-Khammam-Nalgonda Graduates’ constituency, claiming a strong following for its leader and cine actor Pawan Kalyan. But, it has been a traditional stronghold of our party in the constituency,” exclaimed a top leader, pleading anonymity.

Though the central leadership will take a final call, Telangana leaders are expected to put up a stout resistance to ensure one of their own will contest the poll. The plan is to give an opportunity to a prominent leader from the Backward Classes (BC) with the names of teachers’ union leader Biksham Goud, official spokesperson Dr. V. Venkatramana, and young leader Tutupalli Ravi doing the rounds.

According to party sources, the party received around 16 applications for the Warangal-Khammam-Nalgonda seat and 29 for the Hyderabad-Rangareddy-Mahabubnagar constituency. The ‘core’ state leadership group is said to have shortlisted four candidates for each seat for central leadership to take a final decision.

The party views Mr. Ramchander Rao as its strongest candidate and is seen as a leader capable of preventing internal dissatisfaction among aspirants owing to the intense competition for the ticket. He had won the Hyderabad graduates’ constituency election in 2015, defeating the then-ruling BRS when the party was at the peak of its popularity. He later lost to Vani Devi, daughter of former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, who was fielded by the BRS.

The BJP claims to be preparing aggressively for the polls by focusing on voter enrolment. “We expect at least five lakh graduates to register as voters and are confident of putting up a strong performance,” a senior leader said. When contacted, Mr. Ramchander Rao remained non-committal. “The Central Parliamentary Board will take the final decision, most likely next month,” he said.

However, the candidate-selection process has not gone down well with some senior leaders. A party veteran criticised the manner in which the exercise was handled, arguing that if the leadership intended to field the State president, it should have communicated the decision at the outset rather than encouraging multiple aspirants to apply. “There was no effort to talk to the aspirants about their suitability either by the ‘core’ group or the central observors,” he rued. The MLC elections are scheduled to be held in March.

Telangana BJP president N. Ramachander Rao widely seen as the frontrunner for the Hyderabad-Rangareddy-Mahabubnagar Graduates’ constituency

With Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao widely seen as the frontrunner for the Hyderabad-Rangareddy-Mahabubnagar Graduates’ constituency in the upcoming Legislative Council elections, a request from ally Jana Sena Party (JSP) for the other graduates’ seat has triggered unease within the State BJP leadership.

“The JSP has informally sought BJP support for its nominee, Dr. G. Srinivasa Rao, in the Warangal-Khammam-Nalgonda Graduates’ constituency, claiming a strong following for its leader and cine actor Pawan Kalyan. But, it has been a traditional stronghold of our party in the constituency,” exclaimed a top leader, pleading anonymity.

Though the central leadership will take a final call, Telangana leaders are expected to put up a stout resistance to ensure one of their own will contest the poll. The plan is to give an opportunity to a prominent leader from the Backward Classes (BC) with the names of teachers’ union leader Biksham Goud, official spokesperson Dr. V. Venkatramana, and young leader Tutupalli Ravi doing the rounds.

According to party sources, the party received around 16 applications for the Warangal-Khammam-Nalgonda seat and 29 for the Hyderabad-Rangareddy-Mahabubnagar constituency. The ‘core’ state leadership group is said to have shortlisted four candidates for each seat for central leadership to take a final decision.

articles.title: Jordan strikes militant groups in Syria after church attack
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Jordanian military air force jets had “destroyed several terrorist positions” and killed and wounded “numerous members” of groups linked to the perpetrators of the church attack

The Jordanian military said it had struck “terrorist organisations” in neighbouring Syria on Monday (October 26, 2026) in retaliation for a deadly jihadist attack on a church last week, hours after authorities arrested three men they accused of the killings.
It said air force jets had “destroyed several terrorist positions” and killed and wounded “numerous members” of groups linked to the perpetrators of the church attack.
Syrian authorities reported civilian casualties from the raids, with health officials in Daraa province saying six people, including three children and a woman, were killed.
Syria’s civil defence agency reported seven deaths in total, six people in Daraa and one in neighbouring Sweida province.
On Friday (October 23, 2026), gunmen killed nine people during a funeral service at the Greek Orthodox St. George’s Church in the village of Hammoud in Karak governorate, southern Jordan.
Karak is home to a significant Christian community in Muslim-majority Jordan, where Christians make up between two and three percent of the population.

Major General Abdullah al-Maaytah, Jordan’s director of public security, on Monday (October 26, 2026) named the three detained suspects as Hazza Zaidan Mohammed, Meshal Zaidan Mohammed and Ahmad Sami Hussein.
The trio, two of them brothers and the other related by marriage, were cornered at an abandoned house where they had barricaded themselves inside and opened fire on security forces.
“All three terrorists have been injured. They have been taken to hospital and are still receiving treatment,” Mr. Maaytah told a press conference.
One of the suspects was in critical condition, Jordan’s state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka reported. There were no casualties among the security forces, it added.
“This country must remain an oasis of security and stability, and we affirm that Jordan will remain impervious to anyone who dares to challenge it,” Mr. Maaytah said.
Under Jordanian law, murder is punishable by death by hanging.

articles.title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to 60,000 staff, with some Indian teams eligible
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: As major tech giants continue to spend heavily on AI-related investments, concerns persist about the impact of the technology on jobs

Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, the company said on Monday, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant seeks to cut costs while pouring money into artificial intelligence.

Staff on select teams in the United States, Canada, India and Britain at vice president level and below will be eligible, a Microsoft spokesperson said, while some groups of employees, including some working on data centres, sales and marketing, are excluded.

“The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter,” Amy Coleman, an executive vice president and chief people officer, told employees in a memo.
I t’s the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year.
In April, the company reportedly offered around seven percent of its US workforce the option to retire early.
Around 30 percent of those eligible took the voluntary retirement plan, according to CNBC.
Microsoft had 223,000 employees globally at the end of June, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings.
Around 27 percent of Microsoft’s workforce is eligible for the new buyout offer.
The company is expected to report quarterly earnings later this week.
As major tech giants continue to spend heavily on AI-related investments, concerns persist about the impact of the technology on jobs.
Even industry insiders, such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, have warned of mass job losses.
Netflix will reportedly cut around 6 percent of its workforce, or 1,000 jobs, US media reported last week.

articles.title: Bolsonaro’s party says it recognises Lula’s election win in Brazil
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback after trailing Flávio Bolsonaro in a first-round vote, a defeat which fired up the left on the streets and social media to secure him a fourth term in office

Flávio Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party on Monday (October 26, 2026) recognised the outcome of Brazil’s presidential runoff, despite the candidate’s objections to the poll won by leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

Mr. Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), pulled off a dramatic comeback after trailing Mr. Bolsonaro in a first-round vote, a defeat which fired up the left on the streets and social media to secure him a fourth term in office.
In the end, Mr. Lula pulled around 4.4 million more votes than his rival on Sunday (October 25, 2026).

Mr. Bolsonaro, a right-wing senator and 45-year-old son of far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro, cried foul after polling was extended nationwide for two hours, at Mr. Lula’s request, due to transport problems in some cities.
Though Mr. Bolsonaro maintained that he would seek annulment of the presidential election, his party later distanced itself from that position and opted to accept the official vote.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Brazil: Flavio Bolsonaro refuses to concede Lula’s election win

“We recognise the presidential election results, as proclaimed by the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), but we believe that the concerns raised need to be sufficiently addressed within a balanced and democratic political debate,” the party said in a statement late Monday (October 26, 2026).
Flavio Bolsonaro had also requested polling stations stay open in some regions due to heavy rains, but he described the vote extension as “unacceptable” and a “dirty trick.”
While congratulations rolled in for Mr. Lula from world leaders on both sides of the political divide, Mr. Trump, an ally of the Bolsonaro family, said the election “looked terrible to me.”
“I didn’t take sides but it looked like another rigged election frankly,” he told reporters in Washington. “It looked so corrupt.”
ALSO WATCH Watch: Lula defeats far-right Bolsonaro to secure a fourth presidential term | Above the Fold | Oct 26, 2026
In a video posted to social media on Monday (October 26, 2026) afternoon, Mr Bolsonaro said police had ordered him to surrender his passports, adding, “I am now prohibited from leaving the country.”

articles.title: Trump administration asks Washington to set aside ballots from 400 voters it says may be noncitizens
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Justice Department said it had identified 1,500 votes cast by over 400 people in prior elections
The Trump administration on Monday (October 26, 2026) asked Washington state to set aside any ballots received from more than 400 people it suspects registered to vote without U.S. citizenship.

In a letter to the Washington Secretary of State's Office, the Justice Department said it had identified 1,500 votes cast by over 400 people in prior elections. It asked the state to set aside any ballots the people might cast in next month's midterm until state officials can confirm they are legally eligible to vote. The state has more than 5 million registered voters.
“We are asking the state to set aside those ballots until we can confirm they are legal voters,” Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd said in a news conference.

Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs was reviewing the administration's demand. His office noted that it had received about 60 subpoenas from the Justice Department since last month seeking information about voters.

“We take our responsibility to protect voter information seriously and will only respond to requests that follow due process,” Hobbs said in an emailed statement. “We see what's happening in California and don't want Washingtonians to be harassed.”

The effort is the latest by the administration to identify noncitizen voters, even though noncitizen voting is exceptionally rare. President Donald Trump has repeatedly sought to undermine public confidence in elections. The request in Washington is similar to Justice Department attempt to require California to sequester mail ballots from up to 20,000 people the federal government suspects may not be citizens.

California has challenged that, and during rare Sunday arguments, a panel of federal appellate judges questioned the timing, constitutionality and authority of the Justice Department's demand. The Elections Clause of the U.S. Constitution gives state legislatures the power to set the time, place and manner of congressional elections.

Los Angeles County Assistant Registrar-Recorder Monica Flores said in a court filing that her staff went through a sample of 200 records from the Trump administration's list. They found the sample included canceled or inactive registrations, people with no voting history and voters who appeared to have been born in the United States.

The Justice Department told Washington it anticipates sending the state an additional list of people it suspects are not citizens prior to Election Day. It also noted that some of the people it suspects registered without citizenship may have since become naturalized.

Investigations into prior allegations of noncitizen voters have revealed far fewer instances than the Trump administration has claimed. In Nevada, Trump's administration alleged there were 1,500 potential noncitizen voters on the rolls, but subsequent investigation found zero.

In Maricopa County, which includes Phoenix, the county Recorder, who is a Trump supporter, announced that there were 207 possible noncitizens on the county's rolls. The Republican County Attorney determined there were actually eight.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In Maricopa County, which includes Phoenix, the county Recorder, who is a Trump supporter, announced that there were 207 possible noncitizens on the county's rolls. The Republican County Attorney determined there were actually eight.

articles.title: Netanyahu, wanted by ICC, battles for political survival as Israel goes to the polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Public anger over failure to prevent the Hamas attack, an inconclusive war, and the rising costs of living have eroded Netanyahu’s standing at home and abroad; the outcome of this poll is likely to shape the longest-serving PM’s political future, the fate of Likud and the legal challenges he faces

Thousands took to the streets of Tel Aviv on Saturday (October 24, 2026), demanding accountability for the failure to prevent the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack. The anti-government demonstration came just three days ahead of what is being described as one of Israel’s most consequential elections.
The protest adds to the pressure on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose bid to retain power comes amid mounting criticism of his government’s handling of domestic and international issues.

For most of Mr. Netanyahu’s latest term, Israel has been embroiled in one conflict or the other. In less than a year of him taking the seat as Prime Minister in 2022, Israel witnessed the Hamas attack in which more than 1,200 were killed, and about 250 were taken hostage. This stirred concerns and protests over security failure and hostage releases.
Mr. Netanyahu then promised a “total victory” over Hamas and other enemies.

Three years later, the war is still dragging on inconclusively. What began as Israel’s response to the Hamas attack spiralled into an all-out regional conflict in West Asia, with the country launching attacks in Gaza, Iran, Lebanon, Yemen, and Syria.
His involvement of the U.S. in its war against Iran on February 28 has impacted countries much beyond West Asia, as it disrupted global energy supply.

He has also intensified Israel’s operations in the West Bank and has increased settlement projects in the region. This has not only severely impacted his ratings as a Prime Minister but has also isolated Israel internationally.

According to a Pew Research Centre survey conducted earlier this year, majorities in more than thirty surveyed countries expressed unfavourable views of Israel and little or no confidence in Mr. Netanyahu. Even within Israel, the military actions have not alleviated the security concerns. A survey by the Israel Democracy Institute in July this year showed that only a little over one-third of Israelis think that the security situation is better than what it was before ‘Operation Roaring Lion’. The constant state of conflict has also come at severe domestic costs— high inflation, a high cost of living, longer and more exhausting service for Army personnel, a soaring national debt, and declining business investment.
Further, he has been accused of weakening the judiciary and endangering democracy with his far-right government.
For Mr. Netanyahu, the longest-serving Prime Minister seeking the seventh term, a lot is at stake personally too.

According to Arik Rudnitzky, from the Israel Democracy Institute in Jerusalem, these elections are the most decisive political test for Mr. Netanyahu as the leader of the Likud Party. He told The Hindu : “I believe these elections are crucial to the political future of Netanyahu. If he no longer serves as Prime Minister, then he has to face his legal issues, and especially the file is being handled right now in court, with the accusations that he has to defend himself.”

The corruption trial, which began in 2020, has been under way for six years now. Mr. Netanyahu has been indicted on charges of bribery, fraud, and breach of trust. He has, however, denied these charges, and the case continues in court. Without the political power, reports suggest that Mr. Netanyahu would have fewer chances of gaining immunity or reasons to postpone hearings.

articles.title: Anthropic points to AI dangers, soaring sales in IPO filing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The listing would be the first by one of the standalone companies leading the race to build advanced AI, ahead of its main rival OpenAI, the ChatGPT-maker

Anthropic, one of the world's leading artificial intelligence companies, on Monday made public its plans to sell shares on the stock market, revealing soaring sales but also potentially dire safety risks in a major test of whether the AI boom can deliver profits.
Its filing warns investors of dangers ranging from its conflict with the Trump administration to AI systems acting on their own, alongside huge spending commitments on computing power.

The listing would be the first by one of the standalone companies leading the race to build advanced AI, ahead of its main rival OpenAI, the ChatGPT-maker, which has pushed back its own market debut to next year.
It also follows the June listing of SpaceX, which owns Elon Musk's AI venture xAI and saw its shares fall sharply after a strong debut.
A disappointing reception for Anthropic could dent investor enthusiasm for AI, a sector that has become a key driver of the US economy amid worries of a market bubble.
According to The Wall Street Journal, the company is aiming to go public the week of Nov. 16, though the timing could change.

The offering could raise as much as $100 billion in an initial public offering (IPO) that could value Anthropic at between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion, the Wall Street Journal added, citing people familiar with the matter.
The 400-page prospectus devotes over 90 pages to risks specific to an industry that has faced a string of reports in recent months of AI systems behaving in unexpected and harmful ways.

It also reflects the dominant belief among researchers inside Anthropic that AI needs to be developed by a safe pair of hands, or otherwise see its extraordinary powers misused with China having the edge.
The filing cited concerns that advanced systems "could pose catastrophic or existential risks to society if not developed and deployed responsibly."

Anthropic also warned that its "engagement with policymakers and public positions on AI regulation and safety could subject us to heightened scrutiny, political backlash, or disproportionate regulatory action."

The company has been targeted in recent months by the administration of US President Donald Trump for refusing to lift restrictions on how the Pentagon could use its technology, and the Defense Department has since labeled it a national security risk and barred it as a supplier.

articles.title: The Hindu Group, Cancer Institute launch book on comprehensive cancer care
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Cancer 360 examines detection, treatment, rehabilitation and palliation

The Hindu Group, in association with the Cancer Institute (WIA), Adyar, launched Cancer 360: Overview of Detection, Treatment, Palliation , a book examining cancer care from prevention and early detection to treatment, rehabilitation and palliative care. The book was launched at The Hindu office in Chennai.

N. Ram, director of The Hindu Group, launched the book alongside Suresh Nambath, editor of The Hindu . Mr. Ram handed over the first copy to E. Hemanth Raj, executive vice-chairman of Cancer Institute.

Speaking at the launch, Mr. Ram emphasised the importance of making advanced cancer care accessible and affordable. He highlighted the institute’s work in providing treatment to those who need it most and stressed the need to ensure that advances in cancer care reach patients facing barriers to treatment.

Dr. Hemanth Raj spoke about the need to translate advances in cancer research, much of which takes place in the West, into practical interventions in local settings. He also highlighted the institute’s charitable programmes, supported by donations, to help patients access treatment and facilities, and its plans to expand cancer care to reach more patients.
Arvind Krishnamurthy, professor of surgical oncology at Cancer Institute, stressed the need for continued research to improve cancer care and develop better treatments.

The book also addresses care beyond treatment. Mahalakshmi Rangabashyam Shetty, ENT surgeon and lecturer in the Department of Surgical Oncology at the institute, spoke about individualised treatment plans developed through multidisciplinary consultations. She also highlighted the need to tailor exercise and nutrition regimens to individual patients, alongside supportive services such as hospice care.

Surendran Veeraiah, professor and head of the Department of Regional Cancer Centre (RCTC), Cancer Institute, emphasised the importance of psychological support and allied services. He said the book could help make technical information on comprehensive cancer care accessible to more people.

The book features contributions from experts across oncology and allied disciplines. Its chapters cover multidisciplinary tumour boards, psychological care, onco-physiotherapy, palliative care, cancer research, speech and swallowing rehabilitation, early detection, precision treatment, pathology, nutrition and healthcare quality.

articles.title: Plant-based meat yields higher share of absorbable protein than traditional meat: study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Laboratory tests show higher protein bioavailability in five plant-based products than in their chicken counterparts; researchers caution further studies needed to assess health benefits

While plant-derived kababs may still struggle to replicate the taste and texture of meat from a tandoori joint, they may contain relatively more protein in a form that the body can absorb, according to a study presented on Monday (October 26, 2026).

In a collaboration between the CSIR–Institute of Himalayan Bioresource Technology (CSIR-IHBT), Palampur, and the Good Food Institute (GFI) India, a non-profit that promotes alternative proteins such as plant-based, fermentation-derived and cultivated meat, scientists investigated whether protein bioavailability (meaning protein in a form that’s nutritively useful to the body) of traditional meat was the same as that of plant-based meat.

Tests on five cooked plant-based products — two burger patties, a nugget and two seekh kebabs — showed higher bioavailability percentages than their chicken counterparts, according to the findings presented at a press conference on Monday (October 26). The plant-based kebabs scored 80.8% and 86.1% against 38.8% for chicken. The nugget scored 61.2% against 43.4%, and the patties recorded about 57% and 58% against 21.2%.

The findings do not mean plant-based meat is healthier, but only that they are nutritively comparable, as ‘healthier’ is a subjective term, Dr. Padma Ishwarya, senior scientist at GFI India, told The Hindu . “It’s too much of a vague term. It’s too broad a term…for health, we need to do further studies.”

The chicken products held more crude protein and released more amino acids, the building blocks of protein, during digestion, and Dr. Ishwarya said more products and samples would be tested in the next phase.

The work has not yet been published as a journal paper. “It is a report that is hosted on our website, but it is very much peer-reviewed,” Dr. Ishwarya said in a conversation with The Hindu . Two experts reviewed it, she said, and it was an overview and that detailed manuscripts would follow.

Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees, Business Insider reported on Monday (October 26, 2026), citing a company spokesperson.

The company did not immediately comment on the number ‌of employees impacted when contacted by Reuters . The ‌voluntary exit offer ‌will ⁠impact key divisions, including ⁠AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices, ​a source ‌familiar with the matter told Reuters . “This offer will be ⁠available to eligible employees in participating teams in ‌Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below,” Microsoft said in a ‌blog post on Monday (October 26, 2026).
The company ​said it was a time-limited, voluntary program and ⁠built on insights gained ⁠from a previous voluntary retirement program.

articles.title: ECI’s stand that additional declaration is not part of Form 6 comes days after SC said it will examine ‘new’ Form 6
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The ECI has introduced an additional declaration form along with Form 6 which require these voters to provide details of their earlier electoral roll entries or that of their parents or grandparents

The Election Commission of India (ECI) has raised a razor-thin justification to allegations that it has unauthorisedly amended Form 6 to introduce extra-statutory requirements for voters whose names were deleted in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to return to the electoral rolls.

The ECI has introduced an additional declaration form along with Form 6 which require these voters to provide details of their earlier electoral roll entries or that of their parents or grandparents. The ECI calls the exercise ‘mapping’. Any perceived mismatch of lack of detail in this regard is broadly termed as ‘logical discrepancy’. In Delhi alone, there were initially 33.12 lakh cases of ‘no-mapping’ or ‘logical discrepancy’.

Petitioners had claimed in the Supreme Court that the additional declaration form was an illegal amendment to Form 6. ECI cannot have unilaterally altered Form 6. That was the job of the Centre, and not the ECI.
An affidavit displaying a united face among Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi argued that the petitioners had got it wrong.
Form 6 was never changed. The additional declaration form was not part of the statutory Form 6.
“The Declaration is a document provided by SIR orders and is NOT a part of Form 6, which is the statutory Form for inclusion in the electoral roll,” the affidavit said.

The phrase “for inclusion in the electoral roll” does not fully explain the role of Form 6. This Form is meant exclusively to apply as a fresh voter. Petitioners have challenged this aspect too. They argue that pre-existing electors deleted during the SIR exercise are being forced to apply as fresh voters, compelled to do so under the threat of penal consequences.

EC said the additional declaration was part of an online push to assist voters. They could file their required details in a single document rather than produce multiple documents for verification like in the Bihar SIR.

The ECI’s justification has come even as the Supreme Court, on October 12, orally clarified that it had neither approved nor disapproved the controversial alterations made to Form 6 in a May 27 judgment, which was entirely about the legality of the pilot Bihar SIR.
The oral remark had clearly acknowledged the additional declaration form as the “new Form 6”.

“When the Bihar SIR issue was heard and decided, the new Form 6 was not there. The new Form 6 was neither approved nor disapproved by us. But we will examine it now,” Justice Joymalya Bagchi, who is part of the Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, had observed orally.

The remark had come in response to a petition filed by Priya Mishra against the Union government challenging the alterations made to Form 6 to register new voters during the SIR exercises undertaken across multiple States.

articles.title: SIR: Over 99.32 lakh names struck off voter list in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Karnataka’s electorate now stands at 4,55,00,011, down from 5,54,32,314 voters before the SIR began

Karnataka’s final electoral roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has been published, with constituency-wise lists of voters now available on the Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) website. The list can be accessed here .

The State’s electorate now stands at 4,55,00,011, down from 5,54,32,314 voters before the SIR began. More than 99.32 lakh names have been knocked off the rolls, as part of the exercise that was launched with the stated aim of ensuring that every eligible voter was included and every ineligible name removed to achieve a ‘ pure, clean electorate’ .

At the draft stage, the electorate had shrunk from 5.54 crore to 4.46 crore, with over 1.07 crore names deleted. The final roll has seen a net addition of 8.64 lakh names compared with the draft roll. Net additions overall remain far lower than the number of names deleted at the draft stage, leaving close to one crore fewer voters on the final roll than before the SIR.

The final electorate comprises over 2.25 crore male voters, 2.29 crore female voters, and 2,841 third-gender voters. It includes over 6.83 lakh young voters aged 18-19, and more than 3.92 lakh voters aged above 85.

Those who applied for inclusion through Form-6 after September 23, the end of the claims and objections period, will be included in supplementary lists, which will be published every quarter after the SIR. The names of those who applied for inclusion within the claims and objections window will be included in the final roll.
The office of the Chief Electoral Officer of Karnataka has said that an enrolment drive will be taken up after the SIR to add genuine voters whose names were deleted during the exercise.

During the draft roll stage, 16.39 lakh names were deleted on the ground that the voters were dead, while over seven lakh were identified as duplicate entries. Another 3.83 lakh names were deleted under the ‘Others’ category, which is not seen in many other States that conducted the SIR.
Even as the exercise comes to an end, the CEO’s office has not clearly explained what the ‘Others’ category comprises, apart from stating that it includes people who refused to sign.

However, the largest category of deletions — 80.62 lakh names — comprised voters who had shifted residence or were not found at their addresses during the enumeration phase. Unlike those identified as dead or duplicate, these voters were not necessarily ineligible to vote. They would have had to apply through Form 6 to have their names restored to the rolls. Yet, only 7,87,534 applications for inclusion were received, a figure that also includes applications from new voters.

At least 61,059 Form-7 applications seeking the deletion of names from Karnataka’s electoral rolls were filed by election officials themselves, with not a single application mentioning a reason for the deletion , a mandatory requirement under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs), listed as the objectors in these applications, said the system “auto-generated” the forms with their digital signatures when voters could not be reached during hearings on notices issued for no mapping or logical discrepancies, and the voters were therefore marked as “ineligible”.

This meant the same election machinery was raising objections to voters’ names and deciding on whether they should remain on the rolls. Under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 an objection that is not filed in the prescribed manner, including stating the reason, is liable to be rejected.

articles.title: Theni jail escape: Keralam police alerted; combing operations under way in forest areas, says officer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The special teams have shared the pictures of the escaped accused with officers at different locations across Tamil Nadu and Keralam

Following the escape of 17 remand prisoners from a sub-jail in Theni district late on Monday (October 26, 2026) night, the Keralam police were alerted, and combing operations were under way in some forest areas too, said a senior officer in the Tamil Nadu police.

The special teams formed to nab the prisoners have shared their pictures with officers at different locations across Tamil Nadu and Keralam. Searches were under way in the forest areas along the Western Ghats and in the neighbouring Idukki district in Keralam too.

The police identified the warden injured in the attack by the inmates as Thangapandi, a Grade II constable. He has been admitted in the Theni Government Medical College and Hospital. Two others were also undergoing treatment, the senior officer said.

Though the exact locations from where four prisoners were re-apprehended by the special teams were not disclosed immediately, the senior officer said that based on the confessions of the accused, the teams were in the process of nabbing the remaining prisoners who had escaped.
“Once the remaining 13 prisoners are also secured, we will conduct a thorough inquiry,” said Director General of Police Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal.

articles.title: Bangladesh leader raises concerns over Assam forest eviction drive, State minister counters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bangladesh Opposition leader Shafiqur Rahman expressed deep concern over the eviction of Muslim families and demolition of mosques in the State’s Lutumari-Longjap Reserve Forest

Assam Forest Minister Jayanta Mallabaruah on Monday (October 26, 2026) said Bangladesh Opposition leader Shafiqur Rahman’s concerns over an eviction drive at a reserve forest in central Assam were misplaced.
The eviction of 563 families from 314 hectares of land in Nagaon district’s Lutumari-Longjap Reserve Forest on October 17 and 18 were based on Supreme Court directives, he said.
Mr Mallabaruah said the Bangladeshi leader presented a misleading picture of the facts and administrative action, asserting that the eviction drive was a legal and ecological necessity.
Citing Supreme Court directions, including an order dated February 10, he said the court prescribed procedures for eviction from notified forest areas in Assam.
Mr Mallabaruah said the Lutumari-Longjap operation was not an arbitrary administrative exercise and notices were served to the squatters on notified forest land well in advance.

“We deliberately waited for the rainy and flood season to end, recognising the difficulties that displacement can cause to families. The occupants were given time to vacate their homes and remove their belongings. The operation was conducted peacefully, without reported resistance or use of force,” he said.

The Minister rejected allegations that the drive targeted any religious or social community, asserting that it was conducted to reclaim notified forest land rather than target people based on their identity.

He also said Forest personnel would plant indigenous forest species on the reclaimed land to regenerate wildlife habitats, particularly those of elephants, while contributing to efforts to reduce human-elephant conflict.
Mr. Rahman, the chief of the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, said in a social media post on October 24 that the eviction of Muslim families and the demolition of mosques in Assam were deeply concerning.

He said the Assam government demolished the homes of more than 600 Muslim families on October 18 after carrying out a similar exercise the previous day to evict 547 families. “More than 1,100 families were subjected to eviction within just two days. Locals also reported that 10 more mosques were demolished during these eviction drives, some of which were over 50 years old,” the Bangladesh MP had said.

He recalled a Gujarat High Court decision to remove a portion of the 400-year-old Mancha Mosque in Ahmedabad paved the way for its demolition. He also cited the demolition of several ancient mosques and graveyards in Gujarat’s Gir Somnath district in September 2024.

“We are deeply concerned about these incidents. The Indian government is not only failing to protect the rights of Muslim minorities but is also undermining their rights in various ways. Such incidents run counter to humanity, the rule of law, and the values of a civilised society. Regardless of where such actions take place or who is responsible for them, these ill activities must be condemned,” Mr Ahmed said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ECL Chairman and Managing Director Satish Jha confirmed no casualties after workers were stranded in two lifting cages following a pulley system malfunction at the Kumardihi A mine
All 14 workers trapped underground at a coal mine in Paschim Bardhaman district, West Bengal, have been rescued, an official said on Tuesday (October 27, 2026).

The incident occurred on Monday (October 26, 2026), because of a technical glitch in the pulley system at the Kumardihi A underground mine of Eastern Coalfields Ltd. (ECL), a subsidiary of State-run Coal India Ltd.
“All 14 workers have been rescued. There has been no casualty,” Satish Jha, ECL Chairman and Managing Director, said.
The workers were stranded in two lifting cages at a depth of about 50 metres, after a rope slipped out of the pulley drum, disrupting the mechanism used to transport miners.

articles.title: What the new E100 vehicle rules mean | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The amendments modify Rule 115, which deals with emission standards and related requirements for motor vehicles, and Rule 115E, which contains additional provisions relating to emission testing

The story so far: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 , to permit the use of ethanol-based fuels containing up to 100% ethanol (E100) in vehicles. The move paves the way for flex-fuel vehicles, which can run on petrol, ethanol blends of varying proportions, or pure ethanol.
The amendments modify Rule 115, which deals with emission standards and related requirements for motor vehicles, and Rule 115E, which contains additional provisions relating to emission testing.

One of the key changes is the inclusion of E100, or fuel comprising 100% ethanol, alongside E85 in several tables under Rule 115. E85 is a fuel containing up to 85% ethanol, while E100 consists entirely of ethanol, subject to applicable fuel specifications.
The amendments include an explanatory note stating that E85 or E100 may be used only in flex-fuel vehicles designed by original equipment manufacturers.

No. In a press statement, the Ministry sought to allay concerns among motorists, clarifying that a vehicle’s compatibility with E10 or E20 does not establish its suitability for E85. The notification does not require owners of existing vehicles to switch to E85 or modify their vehicles, either now or in the future.

Motorists should check the fuel-compatibility sticker on their vehicle and follow the manufacturer’s guidance in the owner’s manual when choosing fuel at a filling station, the Ministry statement added.

The amendments are expected to facilitate homologation, the official certification process through which authorised agencies, such as the Automotive Research Association of India, verify that vehicles and components comply with technical, safety and environmental standards before they can be approved for sale or use on public roads.
This will help secure type approvals for E100-powered vehicles, supporting their rollout and wider consumer adoption.
Corrections have also been incorporated into fuel classifications, including a reference to gasoline blended with 20% ethanol, or E20, in place of an earlier notation referring to E10.

India achieved its 20% ethanol-blending (E20) target in 2025 , five years ahead of the original 2030 deadline set under the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018. From April 2026, all Bharat Stage-VI (BS-VI) vehicles are required to fully meet E20 emission standards, and all petrol sold across India is mandated to contain 20% ethanol (E20). The policy focus is now widening beyond E20: the government has enabled the regulatory pathway for E85 and E100 vehicles, though these fuels will require compatible flex-fuel vehicles and dedicated dispensing infrastructure.

The main concern is vehicle compatibility. Owners of older or non-E20-compliant vehicles question whether E20 could damage components, raise maintenance costs, or leave them without access to lower-ethanol petrol.

Consumers also question E20’s effect on fuel economy. Ethanol has a lower energy density than petrol; while the government estimates a 5% decline in mileage, some consumers say the loss is greater. Dealers, meanwhile, warn that ethanol’s affinity for water could raise contamination risks during the monsoon, strengthening the case for separate storage and dispensing systems for higher blends. These concerns have prompted calls for a transparent assessment.

articles.title: Israel holds polls amid uncertainty over Netanyahu’s future, coalition numbers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Opposition leaders Gadi Eisenkot and Naftali Bennett are challenging PM Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition, with opinion polls showing neither bloc assured of the 61 seats needed for a majority

Israel is holding parliamentary elections on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeking to retain power amid debate over the government’s handling of the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023, the subsequent wars, and its domestic and foreign policies.

The election is widely seen as a test of Mr. Netanyahu’s leadership, as Opposition leaders, including former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, seek to challenge his right-wing coalition. Opinion polls indicate neither bloc is assured of the parliamentary majority needed to form a government.

Israel, roughly the size of north-eastern India’s Mizoram State, uses a nationwide proportional representation system, with the entire country serving as a single electoral constituency to elect the 120 members of the Knesset, Israel’s parliament.

Voters do not elect individual members of parliament; instead, they vote for closed party lists, a system that allows numerous political parties to compete for seats. To enter the Knesset, a party must cross the 3.25% electoral threshold, a requirement that often prompts pre-election alliances and mergers.

The Knesset serves a four-year term, but elections can be held early if it votes to dissolve itself, fails to approve the State budget within the prescribed period, or a new government cannot be formed.

articles.title: Carney says Trump moving closer to Canada's trade demands as midterms loom
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc's office said Canada remains in “constructive dialogue” with Washington

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday (October 26, 2026) that trade talks with U.S. President Donald Trump's administration have picked up slightly, but any progress is because Washington is moving closer to Canada's demands.
“To the extent any progress has been made, it's because the US is coming closer to our position,” Mr. Carney said.
Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc's office said Canada remains in “constructive dialogue” with Washington.
Mr. Carney described a “slight, slight intensification” of discussions but said Canada's negotiating position remained unchanged.

Asked how he could be sure U.S. President Donald Trump would “sign in pen” this time, after Mr. Carney previously warned that Washington's signature was sometimes “written in pencil,” the Prime Minister replied, “I don't know that.”

Canada rejected Washington's terms in August after the countries appeared close to a deal. Mr. Carney said the offer crossed Canadian “red lines.” Mr. Trump subsequently imposed 50% tariffs on roughly $20 billion in Canadian goods, prompting retaliation and further trade restrictions.

Mr. Trump said on Friday (October 23, 2026) he would lift some 50% tariffs on Canadian goods while imposing new tariffs on dozens of other products. Two days later, he told a Michigan campaign rally that Canada was “willing to give us anything at this moment” and that a deal would be settled “pretty soon.” He told a Detroit television station an agreement could come before the midterms, although it might take months.

Mr. Trump's tariffs have become an issue in closely watched Senate races. Republican candidate Mike Rogers says in a Michigan campaign ad that Canada is “not our enemy” and “we need to end this tariff war now.” In Maine, Republican Sen. Susan Collins pressed the Trump administration to ease tariffs on Canadian goods used by farmers and other businesses, with Washington announcing exemptions on Friday (October 23, 2026).

Mr. Trump has repeatedly complained about the U.S. trade deficit with Canada, but energy accounts for more than the gap. The United States buys millions of barrels of Canadian oil daily, typically at a discount, and runs a trade surplus with Canada when energy is excluded.
Mr. Trump also wants automakers to move production from Canada to the United States, threatening an industry deeply integrated across the border for decades.

Mr. Trump's trade war and repeated threats to make Canada the 51st U.S. state have pushed Mr. Carney to seek new markets, with a goal of doubling Canadian exports outside the United States over the next decade.

Mr. Carney hosts European Union leaders on Thursday and Friday in Montreal to pursue closer economic and security ties. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed making Canada the EU's first associate member, a status that has yet to be defined.

articles.title: U.S.-brokered truce begins in Ukraine city occupied by Russia
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Both Russia and Ukraine said they would observe the truce starting at 3:00 a.m. local time (0100 GMT)

A truce between Ukraine and Russia aimed at allowing humanitarian aid into the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky entered into force early on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), after it was announced by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump last week.
Both sides said they would observe the truce starting at 3:00 a.m. local time (0100 GMT).
AFP was not able to immediately verify whether there had been a decrease in fighting.
And Ukraine’s military said early on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) that ballistic missiles had been launched toward Kyiv.
The war-ravaged city in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region has been caught in middle of the fighting since 2022, when it was seized by Russian forces at the start of their invasion.
Former residents told AFP earlier this year that those remaining in the city were starving, lacked medicine and could not easily leave.
The Russian Ministry of Defence said on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) that the truce was in effect.

“In connection with preparations for a humanitarian operation in the area of Oleshky, Kherson Oblast, (Russian forces) have ceased fire in the Kherson sector and introduced a ‘regime of silence’,” the ministry said on its Telegram channel.
Kyiv’s human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said Ukraine was “fulfilling its commitments” to the ceasefire.
“The sides are adhering to the agreements that we reached,” he said on Telegram.
The ceasefire, which applies to a limited area, comes as the Ukraine war grinds through its fifth year.
Three-way peace talks between Washington, Moscow and Kyiv are set to resume in November after a months-long hiatus.

articles.title: A guide to Israel’s elections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Israelis will go to the polls on October 27 in the first general election since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack. The election will determine not only the fate of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu but also the country’s direction amid deep internal divisions, regional security challenges and international isolation. Mr. Netanyahu’s central campaign promise is that only his government can guarantee Israel’s security. His opponents, led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief, question his failure to prevent the October 7 attack. Mr. Eisenkot has also pledged to end the “forever wars” and repair Israel’s relations with global powers.
Who is Gadi Eisenkot, the man who challenges King Bibi? Read this profile .

Israel is known for its fractious politics. The Knesset, the country’s 120-member parliament, has never seen a single party win an outright majority of 61 seats, making coalition-building a defining feature of Israeli politics. The country holds elections every four years, provided a parliament completes its term. Mr. Netanyahu’s rightwing Likud, which won 32 seats in the 2022 parliamentary elections, has arguably been the dominant political party for years. Mr. Netanyahu, the country’s longest serving Prime Minister, has also maintained a tight grip over the party. In the 2022 elections, the Likud-led right-religious coalition, including Religious Zionism, Otzma Yehudit, Shas and United Torah Judaism won a majority and Mr. Netanyahu formed the government.

The last four years were extremely consequential for Israel. After the Hamas attack, Israel launched a disastrous war in Gaza. It is today facing allegations of committing genocide against Palestinians.Israel also widened the war in Gaza into a regional conflict, targeting Iran’s allies before striking Tehran itself, first in June 2025 and again in February 2026. Despite the succession of wars, many of Israel’s security challenges remain unresolved. Hamas remains in the parts of Gaza where Palestinians have been pushed to. Hezbollah was forced to retreat from southern Lebanon, but the Shia group remains a powerful socio-political militant outfit in Lebanon. In Syria, the government of Bashar al-Assad, an Iranian ally, collapsed. But the man who replaced Mr. Assad was Ahmad al Sharaa, a former al-Qaeda commander who is today a close ally of Turkey, another regional Israeli rival. The war against Iran has reached nowhere, with the Islamic Republic not only surviving the initial strikes but also retaliating with attacks on Israel and U.S. bases across the Persian Gulf.
To understand the security challenges Israel is facing despite its back-to-back wars, watch this episode of Global Faultlines: Is Israel winning?

Inside Israel-Palestine, settler politicians, including National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir (Otzma Yehudit) and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich (Religious Zionism) have supported new settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories. Settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank has escalated in recent years.

It was against this background Mr. Eisenkot built his campaign on a strong anti-Netanyahu platform. His Yashar party has made significant progress over the past year. According to most opinion polls, Likud’s tally is expected to fall from last election’s 32 while Yashar could emerge as the single largest party. In Israel, which doesn’t have a Constitution, the President usually invites the leader of the largest party to form the government. That leader typically gets 28 days to hold talks with other parties and stitch together a coalition with the support of at least 61 Members of the Knesset (MKs).

This year, although Mr. Eisenkot’s party is expected to win most seats, forming a coalition is not going to be easy for him. Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, despite political differences, is ideologically more coherent than the centrist coalition Mr. Eisenkot wants to build. The United Torah Judaism, which left the coalition government last year, could support Mr. Netanyahu after the elections. But it’s unclear whether the Likud coalition, even with the support of the UTJ, would pass the 61-seat threshold.

On the other side, the opposition is filled with heavyweights. Besides Mr. Eisdenkot’s Yashar, the Democrats, led by former deputy military chief Yair Golan; the Yisrael Beiteinu of former Finance Minister Avigdor Lieberman and the Together alliance, led by former Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, are the key players in the opposition. Mr. Eisdenkot’s challenge is to bring all of them together–some of them such as Mr. Bennett and Mr. Lieberman, nourish their own prime ministerial ambitions.

Opinion polls suggest that even if all these parties come together, they would still fall short of a majority. Mr. Eisdenkot may have to take the support – either direct or outside support – of the Arab Raam party. As of now, he has maintained that he would not join hands with the Arab parties. If he takes direct support from Raam after the elections, it would provide a political weapon to Mr. Netanyahu even before the government is formed. If Mr. Eisenkot or any of his allies forms a minority government with the outside support of Arabs, it would be a weak government.

In many ways, this is going to be one of the most consequential elections in Israel’s history. Mr. Netanyahu’s appeal is waning, but he is not out yet. The opposition wants to build a political alternative, but they face structural challenges in a polity that has clearly shifted rightward. Meanwhile, all mainstream politicians, from Mr. Netanyahu to Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Bennett, agree that a Palestine state should not be formed under any condition.

In the latest episode of Global Faultlines , I answer audience questions, mostly on West Asia. The crisis in the region seems to be deepening with rapid escalation of the war between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis and the growing possibility of a new round of Israeli-U.S. strikes on Iran. It’s bad news for the global energy markets. Bad news for the global economy. And bad news for India.

Mr. Eisdenkot’s challenge is to bring all of them together–some of them such as Mr. Bennett and Mr. Lieberman, nourish their own prime ministerial ambitions.

Opinion polls suggest that even if all these parties come together, they would still fall short of a majority. Mr. Eisdenkot may have to take the support – either direct or outside support – of the Arab Raam party. As of now, he has maintained that he would not join hands with the Arab parties. If he takes direct support from Raam after the elections, it would provide a political weapon to Mr. Netanyahu even before the government is formed. If Mr. Eisenkot or any of his allies forms a minority government with the outside support of Arabs, it would be a weak government.

In many ways, this is going to be one of the most consequential elections in Israel’s history. Mr. Netanyahu’s appeal is waning, but he is not out yet. The opposition wants to build a political alternative, but they face structural challenges in a polity that has clearly shifted rightward. Meanwhile, all mainstream politicians, from Mr. Netanyahu to Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Bennett, agree that a Palestine state should not be formed under any condition.

In the latest episode of Global Faultlines , I answer audience questions, mostly on West Asia. The crisis in the region seems to be deepening with rapid escalation of the war between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis and the growing possibility of a new round of Israeli-U.S. strikes on Iran. It’s bad news for the global energy markets. Bad news for the global economy. And bad news for India.

The election will determine not only the fate of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu but also the country’s direction amid deep internal divisions, regional security challenges and international isolation. Mr. Netanyahu’s central campaign promise is that only his government can guarantee Israel’s security. His opponents, led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief, question his failure to prevent the October 7 attack. Mr. Eisenkot has also pledged to end the “forever wars” and repair Israel’s relations with global powers.

articles.title: How community-based weather data is bolstering this Wayanad panchayat’s demand for drought-hit status
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Monitoring network helps Thirunelly panchayat to track hyperlocal variability in rainfall patterns and plan timely interventions. It has urged Keralam government to declare the area severely drought-hit amid concerns over a strong El Niño

A community-based weather monitoring system set up by Thirunelly grama panchayat in Wayanad, Keralam, has recorded a 47% deficit in southwest monsoon rainfall, prompting the local body to urge the Keralam government to declare the area severely drought-hit amid concerns over a strong El Niño.

The network comprises rain gauges installed in all wards and at select public institutions and offices, with 15 trained volunteers regularly recording weather data. The initiative, implemented with technical support from the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology, enables the panchayat to track hyperlocal variations in rainfall and respond to emerging agricultural and water security concerns.
The data collected through the system have helped the panchayat assess the severity of the rainfall deficit during the current season.

“The monitoring network has been helping us better understand local conditions, and what we are witnessing in this region is unprecedented,” said Thirunelly grama panchayat president Anju Balan. “The lack of rain has severely affected paddy cultivation, forcing many farmers to abandon it midway. Coffee, pepper and other crops have also been adversely affected. The panchayat has also started facing water shortages.”

The India Meteorological Department’s (IMD) lone weather station in Wayanad, located at Ambalavayal, recorded a 53% deficit in the southwest monsoon rainfall during the same period. Eastern Wayanad has been particularly affected, with paddy fields drying up and agricultural activities coming under stress.

The Hume Centre’s weather laboratory, which monitors meteorological conditions at 200 locations across Wayanad, recorded a rise of more than 2°C in Thirunelly’s average maximum temperature in September compared with the same month in 2025. The higher temperatures have compounded the stress on crops caused by inadequate rainfall.
Average maximum temperature in Thirunelly over the past three years. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

C.K. Vishnudas, executive director of the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology, says the panchayat’s initiative shows how community-based climate monitoring can inform local governance and enable timely interventions.

“The data collected at the local level have helped the panchayat assess the situation and make a demand based on evidence. This is a bottom-up approach to climate monitoring and decision-making,” he said.
Paddy farmers in the region had observed early flowering, reportedly due to heat stress.

“The failure of the southwest monsoon has affected agricultural operations and crop growth during the crucial transplanting and early growth stages of paddy,” said Rajesh Krishnan, chief executive officer of the Thirunelly Agri Producer Company. “Although recent northeast monsoon rains have brought some relief to Wayanad, the prolonged rainfall deficit has left farmers concerned about the kharif season. If the situation persists, they could suffer substantial yield losses.”

Against this backdrop, the panchayat has written to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, who is also the chairperson of the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority, seeking urgent intervention to provide relief to affected communities, including paddy and dairy farmers and plantation crop growers.

articles.title: Why West Bengal’s C-Sections, at nearly 1 in 2 births, demand a hard look
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: NFHS-6 data puts the rate of Caesarean sections in West Bengal at 44.5%, nearly double the 2015-16 level and significantly higher than the national average of 27.2%. Private facilities handle about 3 in 10 births but perform almost 6 in 10 of the operations

On September 29, 2015, a memo went out from Swasthya Bhawan, the West Bengal Health Department’s headquarters in Salt Lake, to every medical college principal and every district’s chief medical officer of health. Its subject was a concern the Union Health Ministry had raised about rising Caesarean sections rates, especially where the operation was not medically needed.

The memo enclosed a statement the World Health Organization (WHO) had issued that April. It suggested that chief medical officers, who license private clinics, carry out periodic “prescription audits” of Caesareans in private and government facilities.

At the time, the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-4, 2015-16) had found that about one in four births were Caesareans in West Bengal (23.8%). The latest sixth round (NFHS-6, 2023-24) puts the figure at 44.5%, close to double that level, against 27.2% for India. In Kolkata and North 24 Parganas it was found to be 67.5%, meaning about two of every three babies were born via a C-section.

A Caesarean section saves mothers and babies when labour goes wrong. It is also, however, major abdominal surgery, with slower recovery rates and higher risks of infection and bleeding, and it leaves a scar that can complicate later pregnancies.

The WHO statement said that across a population, Caesarean rates above 10% are not associated with fewer deaths of mothers or newborns. While the WHO does not recommend a specific rate , the increasing numbers of Caesarean births in West Bengal, and more widely in India, deserve attention.
The NFHS’s first three rounds, from 1992-93 to 2005-06, found West Bengal close to the national average when it came to C-sections, at 10.2% against 8.5% by the third NFHS round.

The State then pulled away. Its rate reached 32.6% in NFHS-5, for which West Bengal was surveyed in 2019-21, and by NFHS-6 (2023-24) the gap with India had widened from 1.7 percentage points in 2005-06 to 17.3.
The climb has also grown steeper. The rise of 13.6 points between 2005-06 and 2015-16 took a decade, while the latest 11.9 points came in four to five years.
The data cannot reveal how many of West Bengal’s operations were necessary, though it does show when and where the rise happened.

Of every 10 women who give birth in a private facility in West Bengal, 9 nine now have a C-section (87.7%). In 2015-16, the year of the memo, the figure was 70.9%. West Bengal’s numbers are also significantly higher than current the national private-sector rate, 54.1%.

While numbers in the government sector are lower, they are also on the rise: government facilities performed C-sections in 28.8% of the births they handled, up from 18.8% in 2015-16 and 1.7 times the national public-sector figure of 16.9%. In Kolkata, the share of births in government facilities delivered by C-section rose from 32.4% in NFHS-5 to 59.1% in NFHS-6.
Births are also increasingly moving to private facilities. Between NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 their share of the total rose from about 19% to about 29%, even as the public share fell from 72.4% to 65.8%.

articles.title: Remembering Chef Damu: A life dedicated to Tamil Nadu’s culinary heritage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A tribute to the late Chef K Damodaran, who took Tamil Nadu’s cuisine to the world stage, documented forgotten dishes, shared cooking techniques through his television shows, and inspired thousands with his simple, no-nonsense approach to food
I was planning on calling him for a story on traditional Deepavali snacks this week. But it was not meant to be.

Every year, come festive season, Chef K Damodaran’s is the first name that comes to my mind for recipes and Tamil Nadu food trends. ‘Hello Akila, eppidi irukeenga?’ he would ask, and I would feel a pang of guilt for reaching out only when I needed something from him. But he would put me at ease by readily launching forth into the subject.

I spoke to him last in April this year for a story on the summer cooler kambankoozh . A lot of people who knew him and worked closely with him, are still processing his passing. Chef Damu passed away in Chennai on October 25. He was 72.
Culinary expert Chef Damu tasting a preparation at The Hindu Our State Our Taste cookery competition held at Hotel Atithi in Puducherry. | Photo Credit: SINGARAVELOU T

From the Tamil Nadu Deepavali tradition of eating idli with mutton curry for breakfast to a recipe he documented from an 80-year-old in a village near Palayamkottai, Chef Damu has shared several gems with me over the past decade.

In October 2016, he shared his experiences working with noon meal cooks from 25 Government schools in villages in Srirangam district. He made vegetable biryani and masala muttai for 350 children. “There was an increase in their attendance the next day,” he recalled with enthusiasm. He taught noon meal workers to make tomato biryani, chickpea pulao, vegetable biryani, bisibelabhath, keerai rice, tomato, masala and pepper egg.

In 2019, he travelled to 15 cities in Tamil Nadu, tasting hundreds of dishes that participants made as part of The Hindu ’s Our State Our Taste cookery competition . It was a monumental task, but he made it seem so easy. Chef Damu loved food, often, the kind that did not need elaborate masalas and marination. As a TV chef, he showed how a masala base of onion, tomato, ginger and garlic, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powder, was enough to elevate anything from brinjal to chicken.

I remember seeing his cooking shows and how he would not make a big fuss about measurements, instead going by what his hands and eyes told him. He would crush tomatoes by hand before adding them to the simmering kuzhambu, cooking in his favourite clay tawa. “This dish will go well with rasam or sambar rice,” he would say as he scooped it onto a waiting banana leaf that the camera would zoom into. I have never actually tried chicken fry with sambar rice, but have always wanted to, like Damu had suggested.
Chef Damu demonstrating recipes at Gramathu Virundhu Food Festival held at GRTGrand Hotel in Chennai | Photo Credit: RAGU R

Remembering Chef Damu: A life dedicated to Tamil Nadu’s culinary heritage

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

A tribute to the late Chef K Damodaran, who took Tamil Nadu’s cuisine to the world stage, documented forgotten dishes, shared cooking techniques through his television shows, and inspired thousands with his simple, no-nonsense approach to food

I was planning on calling him for a story on traditional Deepavali snacks this week. But it was not meant to be.

Every year, come festive season, Chef K Damodaran’s is the first name that comes to my mind for recipes and Tamil Nadu food trends. ‘Hello Akila, eppidi irukeenga?’ he would ask, and I would feel a pang of guilt for reaching out only when I needed something from him. But he would put me at ease by readily launching forth into the subject.

I spoke to him last in April this year for a story on the summer cooler kambankoozh . A lot of people who knew him and worked closely with him, are still processing his passing. Chef Damu passed away in Chennai on October 25. He was 72.

Culinary expert Chef Damu tasting a preparation at The Hindu Our State Our Taste cookery competition held at Hotel Atithi in Puducherry. | Photo Credit: SINGARAVELOU T

From the Tamil Nadu Deepavali tradition of eating idli with mutton curry for breakfast to a recipe he documented from an 80-year-old in a village near Palayamkottai, Chef Damu has shared several gems with me over the past decade.

In October 2016, he shared his experiences working with noon meal cooks from 25 Government schools in villages in Srirangam district. He made vegetable biryani and masala muttai for 350 children. “There was an increase in their attendance the next day,” he recalled with enthusiasm. He taught noon meal workers to make tomato biryani, chickpea pulao, vegetable biryani, bisibelabhath, keerai rice, tomato, masala and pepper egg.

In 2019, he travelled to 15 cities in Tamil Nadu, tasting hundreds of dishes that participants made as part of The Hindu ’s Our State Our Taste cookery competition . It was a monumental task, but he made it seem so easy. Chef Damu loved food, often, the kind that did not need elaborate masalas and marination. As a TV chef, he showed how a masala base of onion, tomato, ginger and garlic, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powder, was enough to elevate anything from brinjal to chicken.

I remember seeing his cooking shows and how he would not make a big fuss about measurements, instead going by what his hands and eyes told him. He would crush tomatoes by hand before adding them to the simmering kuzhambu, cooking in his favourite clay tawa. “This dish will go well with rasam or sambar rice,” he would say as he scooped it onto a waiting banana leaf that the camera would zoom into. I have never actually tried chicken fry with sambar rice, but have always wanted to, like Damu had suggested.

Chef Damu demonstrating recipes at Gramathu Virundhu Food Festival held at GRTGrand Hotel in Chennai | Photo Credit: RAGU R

“He has mentored lakhs of students,” says Sheetharam Prasaad, corporate executive chef with GRT Hotels and Resorts. While Damu’s work in Tamil Nadu cuisine is well-known, Sheetharam points out that as part of SICA, Damu was involved in a lot of charity work. “I remember his dedication when he was training noon meal workers. He taught them safety and hygiene standards they are sure to remember for life,” he says.

He taught them safety and hygiene standards they are sure to remember for life,” he says.

articles.title: Highways Department begins repair of Chennai roads
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Tamil Nadu Highways Department has kept 5,000 bags of cold mix ready for repairing roads that have been damaged by the rains in Chennai the previous week.

The damage to Major Mukund Varadarajan Road (Velachery-Tambaram Road) has been given priority, as the road cut made by the CMWSSB to lay a water pipeline of 2-metre diameter over a stretch of 800 metres had to be restored.

Almost all roads maintained by the Highways Department have suffered some kind of damage due to water stagnation or rainwater falling from Chennai Metro Rail pillars. In some places, the top layer has worn off, while in others, potholes have developed.

Gowri, a resident of Thoraipakkam, said that a few stretches on Rajiv Gandhi Salai beyond Sholinganallur were in a bad condition. “Movement of vehicles is slowing down considerably due to the bad patches. Schoolchildren are the worst affected as they have to reach their institutions early in the day when it is still raining,” she pointed out.

Kumar, a driver, said that the Kamakshi Hospital junction was in urgent need of repairs, given the volume of vehicles that pass through the junction to reach Madipakkam, Tambaram, or Velachery. “Stretches of the Velachery-Tambaram Road in Pallikaranai have also been damaged extensively. The damage is evident in places where widening has not been completed and the road is narrow. There is no way for the rainwater to drain away, as these locations do not have stormwater drains,” he pointed out. Land acquisition has been moving at a slow pace because some property owners have approached the courts.

Of the 650-km network of roads under Chennai City roads, 43 km have suffered damage. Places like Moovarasampet and Nanmangalam, which lack stormwater drains, have suffered significant damage. Sources in the Highways Department said they were taking up repairs wherever necessary. “We have mobilised the men and machinery needed for the repairs. We are waiting for a dry spell before the cold mix is used. Temporary pothole-filling work is also under way,” the source added.
