articles.title: To make AI morally good, tech companies are turning to religion, in spite of doubts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Tech companies are increasingly turning to religion for guidance on developing ethical AI models
As tech companies race to build the most powerful artificial intelligence, some are also asking how to teach a chatbot right from wrong. Their answer? Religion.

“These are not questions a lab can answer,” Anthropic co-founder Chris Olah said earlier this year at the Vatican’s presentation of Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI. “They are questions traditions like yours have carried for millennia.”

Amid this much-discussed turn to faith, there has been little public scrutiny surrounding what exactly these technology companies think religion is — and, perhaps more important, what they hope to get out of it.

As executives sound the alarm about AI's destructive potential and debate the need to develop morally good models, they are increasingly seeking input from philosophers and faith leaders. The executives' philosophy goes something like this: that religion can help inform AI to be morally good in an environment where fears about it — founded and unfounded — are hopscotching across the culture.

Because these companies are not bound to a particular religion, the goal is often quite broad — an aggregate of moral ideas that can inform their models. “What I think ChatGPT should do is reflect that weighted average, or whatever, of humanity’s moral view,” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said last year.

But experts and adherents alike warn that this idea fails to reckon with how different traditions and worldviews can often contradict one another. In short, they say, it's not exactly how religion works.

For decades, scholars have pushed back against a widespread view of religion as a set of rules or principles that can be divorced from the “messy, practical, ad hoc” ways adherents live, argues Webb Keane, an anthropologist at the University of Michigan.

The idea that religion can be separated from things like culture and politics remains entrenched, even though it suffuses both in many ways. Some worry that AI companies, as they ask various faith leaders to answer ethical questions, will further perpetuate a theory of religion that fails to recognise the importance of doctrine, ritual and relationships.

Here's the issue, Keane argues: If you assume that religion overall can offer a distinct set of extractable moral principles, using it to train AI risks prioritising certain traditions and distorting others — particularly when it comes to faiths that do not see themselves primarily as a system of ethics.

“There’s a very conventional way of thinking of religion as a rule book,” he said. “It is certainly very tied to scriptural religion, and the scriptural religions at the end of the day really turn out to be the Abrahamic religions.”

That’s not to say these meetings have lacked diverse representation. Nor does it suggest that their engagement with religion hasn’t been thoughtful from the perspective of those in attendance, like Meghan Sullivan, a philosopher of religion who leads an initiative on ethics and AI at the University of Notre Dame.

Though it doesn't enumerate the traditions it has consulted, Anthropic said in a May blog post that they’d met with “scholars, clergy, philosophers and ethicists from more than 15 religious and cross-cultural groups” — a pool they hope to broaden in the future.

articles.title: Hyderabad’s drinking water sources Singur and Manjira reservoirs decline, Telangana to divert Godavari water
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Pipeline interconnection works are underway near Velimela village, close to the Outer Ring Road to link the 3,000-mm-diameter Godavari ring main with the 1,200-mm-diameter Manjira Phase-III and IV gravity main pipelines

The State government on Sunday decided to divert Godavari water to meet the drinking water needs of areas in Hyderabad that depend on the Singur and Manjira reservoirs, which are fast declining. The move is aimed at averting shortages and preparing for a possible acute water crisis in the coming months amid El Nino conditions.

Following Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s directions, the Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) has initiated work to interconnect existing pipelines to facilitate the diversion.

As part of the plan, pipeline interconnection works are underway near Velimela village, close to the Outer Ring Road to link the 3,000-mm-diameter Godavari ring main with the 1,200-mm-diameter Manjira Phase-III and IV gravity main pipelines. The interconnection is expected to enable Godavari water to be diverted into the Singur–Manjira supply network as required.
Works underway in Velimela village to link 3,000-mm-diameter Godavari ring main with the 1,200-mm-diameter Manjira Phase-III and IV gravity main pipelines. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT

HMWSSB Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy is overseeing the preparations. The Board’s Technical Director Prabhu and Chief General Manager Rajashekhar inspected the works at Velimela on Sunday and reviewed their progress.

Once the interconnection works are completed, Godavari water can be supplied to areas served by the Singur–Manjira system, and help reduce the risk of drinking water supply disruptions during periods of scarcity.

articles.title: SC says 14 States so far agree to raise retirement age of Judicial Officers from 60 to 62 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The CJI said that so far 14 States have agreed to raise the retirement age to 62 years and "we are hopeful that others will also follow"

The Supreme Court on Monday expressed satisfaction that as many as 14 States have agreed to r aise the retirement age of District Judicial Officers from 60 to 62 years and refused to list for urgent hearing the separate pleas of Judges who are on the verge of retiring or have just retired.

"This pertains to the persuasive jurisdiction of this court. The issue is between the Supreme Court and the states," a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said while declining to list individual pleas of Judges who have to demit office after reaching the age of 60 years.

The CJI said that so far 14 States have agreed to raise the retirement age to 62 years and "we are hopeful that others will also follow." The bench said though it has listed the petition for hearing, it did not approve the moving of individual pleas by Judicial Officers.
Senior advocate Ranjit Kumar mentioned the plea for listing saying that Judicial Officers are retiring every day.
On September 4, the Bench had directed States to raise the retirement age of Judicial Officers from 60 to 62 years.

The Bench had said Judicial Officers in the seven States — Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal — have superannuated on or after March 31 this year shall be given an option to re-join the judicial office, if they have not already obtained subsequent employment.

These States, which have consented to the enhancement of age of the Judicial Officers, are directed to amend the service rules and extend the age of superannuation in the judicial service to 62 years, subject to the suitability assessment of the concerned Judicial Officer by the High Court, the Bench had said, adding such amendments shall be carried out preferably within two months.

"Pending amendment of the rules, no Judicial Officer in the aforesaid States who has attained the age of 60 years shall superannuate until he attains the age of 62 years, subject to an assessment of his suitability and performance by the High Court concerned," it had said.

The Supreme Court had directed Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam,Bihar, Goa, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Keralam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha, Punjab, Rajasthan, Telangana, Tripura, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, NCT of Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry to reconsider their decision on enhancing retirement age of judicial officers.

Earlier, the Bench had said that States cannot cite financial burden to oppose raising the retirement age of Judicial Officers. It had asked State governments to revisit the issue of enhancing the age of superannuation of Judges.
The Bench was hearing a petition seeking uniform enhancement of the retirement age of District Judiciary Judges from 60 to 62 years across the country.
While the retirement age of Supreme Court judges is 65, the High Court Judges superannuate at the age of 62 years.

articles.title: How are tropical cyclones named?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tropical cyclones are the second-most dangerous natural hazards, after earthquakes

The cyclonic storm that is brewing over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ and is likely to intensify into a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on the morning of October 27, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

The climate-monitoring agency says that the storm is “very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal by midnight of today, the 26th October and into a very severe cyclonic storm over the same region on 27th October. Thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph by forenoon of 28th October, 2026.”
The severe cyclonic storm will make landfall between the northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha coasts on the morning of October 28.
A tropical cyclone is a rapidly rotating storm that begins over a tropical ocean and can vary in speed, size, and intensity. They are also called hurricanes or typhoons, depending on the region.
Tropical cyclones are the second-most dangerous natural hazards, after earthquakes, according to the World Meteorological Organisation.
The WMO elaborates that the process of determining names for tropical cyclones is conducted by the relevant tropical cyclone regional body at its annual or biennial session.
There are five tropical cyclone regional bodies, which are

These bodies establish pre-designated lists of names, the procedures for which can vary, with some regions using alphabetical order and others using the alphabetical order of country names. No tropical cyclone is named after an individual.

The WMO adds that the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre (RSMC) New Delhi Tropical Cyclone Centre is responsible for naming the tropical cyclones that have formed over the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea when they have reached the relevant intensity.

Cyclones that form in the Northern Indian Ocean are named in a cyclical fashion by thirteen countries — Bangladesh, India, Iran, Maldives, Myanmar, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Thailand, United Arab Emirates, and Yemen.
The classification of a tropical cyclone depends on its maximum sustained wind speed. They are designated as follows
1. Tropical depression is when the maximum sustained windspeed is less than 63 km/hour.

articles.title: Natural gas leak from ONGC pipeline in Andhra’s Konaseema; work on to plug the leak
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: All wells operated by the ONGC in the area are closed until the leak is plugged and a new pipeline is laid

Safety personnel of the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) are working to plug a natural gas leak from a pipeline near Machavaram village in Ambajipeta mandal of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district. Local residents reported a minor gas leak at around 8.30 a.m. on Monday, (October 26, 2026).

ONGC authorities, who are coordinating the operation, told The Hindu : “Our own Safety wing personnel are involved in plugging the natural gas leak from the pipeline and later the existing pipeline will be replaced today itself. The fire was completely under control by 11.20 a.m.”

They added: “All the wells operated by the ONGC are closed temporarily until the leakage is plugged and new pipeline is laid. We are coordinating with the district officials to update about the progress of the work.”
In a release, District Collector R. Mahesh Kumar said the fire was under control and efforts were on to plug the leak.

In January this year, a blowout at the ONGC’s Mori-5 well at Irusumanda village in Malkipuram mandal of the same district led to a fire with flames rising up to 25 metres. People living around the well were evacuated and about 75 coconut trees and crops on three acres were damaged before the well was brought under control.
In July 2025, natural gas leaked from a well being drilled by the ONGC at Pasarlapudi Lanka in Mamidikuduru mandal, and the district officials ordered the drilling to be stopped.

Natural gas leak from ONGC pipeline in Andhra’s Konaseema; work on to plug the leak

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

All wells operated by the ONGC in the area are closed until the leak is plugged and a new pipeline is laid

Safety personnel of the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) are working to plug a natural gas leak from a pipeline near Machavaram village in Ambajipeta mandal of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district. Local residents reported a minor gas leak at around 8.30 a.m. on Monday, (October 26, 2026).

ONGC authorities, who are coordinating the operation, told The Hindu : “Our own Safety wing personnel are involved in plugging the natural gas leak from the pipeline and later the existing pipeline will be replaced today itself. The fire was completely under control by 11.20 a.m.”

They added: “All the wells operated by the ONGC are closed temporarily until the leakage is plugged and new pipeline is laid. We are coordinating with the district officials to update about the progress of the work.”

In a release, District Collector R. Mahesh Kumar said the fire was under control and efforts were on to plug the leak.

In January this year, a blowout at the ONGC’s Mori-5 well at Irusumanda village in Malkipuram mandal of the same district led to a fire with flames rising up to 25 metres. People living around the well were evacuated and about 75 coconut trees and crops on three acres were damaged before the well was brought under control.

In July 2025, natural gas leaked from a well being drilled by the ONGC at Pasarlapudi Lanka in Mamidikuduru mandal, and the district officials ordered the drilling to be stopped.

1. Core Context & Background: All wells operated by the ONGC in the area are closed until the leak is plugged and a new pipeline is laid

Ambedkar Konaseema district. Local residents reported a minor gas leak at around 8.30 a.m. on Monday, (October 26, 2026).

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In July 2025, natural gas leaked from a well being drilled by the ONGC at Pasarlapudi Lanka in Mamidikuduru mandal, and the district officials ordered the drilling to be stopped.

articles.title: Human-wildlife conflict: Preventive measures on the cards around hotspots in Keralam’s Perambra estate
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Latest intervention comes amid sharp escalation in wild animal incursions across Peruvannamuzhi forest range, impacting Chakkittapara, Muthukad and surrounding plantation belts. Local residents and workers point out that the situation has become critical, particularly during early-morning hours when rubber tapping takes place

In the wake of recurring wild elephant attacks and mounting safety threats at the Plantation Corporation’s Perambra Estate at Chakkittapara in Kozhikode district of Keralam, local people’s representatives and authorities have stepped in with a series of urgent preventive measures.

Following a recent incident where a woman plantation worker sustained injuries while narrowly escaping a wild elephant, local representatives visited the affected families to assess the ground situation and reassure the workforce.

To address the immediate threats, authorities have secured assurances from the estate manager that the construction of protective fencing around the Perambra Estate boundaries will commence at the earliest to block the entry of wild animals.

Additionally, strict instructions have been issued to Forest department officials to scale up patrolling and monitor vulnerable plantation sectors. High-level discussions were also held between local body members, the Perambra Estate manager, and frontline forest department officials to streamline security protocols and ensure the safety of the workforce.

The latest intervention comes amidst a sharp escalation in wild animal incursions across the Peruvannamuzhi forest range, severely impacting Chakkittapara, Muthukad, and the surrounding plantation belts.

The recent victim, T.K. Usha, 48, a rubber tapper from Chengottukolly, Muthukad, was working in the estate when a charging wild elephant targeted her. While fleeing in panic, she suffered a fall and sustained injuries before being rushed to a private hospital in Chakkittapara.

Local residents and workers point out that the situation has become critical, particularly during the early-morning hours when rubber tapping takes place. Because elephants often lurk undetected deep within the plantation vegetation, workers face the constant danger of running directly into them. The crisis was further highlighted just days earlier when a Forest department watcher stationed at the Perambra Plantation Corporation estate suffered severe injuries in a similar wild elephant attack.

Beyond the threat to human life, the unchecked animal straying has caused extensive economic damage to the nearby farmers. Herds of wild elephants have been destroying decades-old rubber trees, breaking branches, and uprooting crops. This widespread crop destruction has inflicted financial losses running into lakhs of rupees, threatening the very livelihood of local farmers and estate workers.

In response to the growing unrest, estate officials clarified that preventive measures are being strengthened. Management sources say that areas previously enclosed with solar fencing have seen a significant reduction in wild elephant intrusions. Consequently, work on installing new solar fencing will begin immediately in the heavily affected hotspots where elephant herds frequently break through.

Meanwhile, locals continue to demand the immediate extension of existing safety barriers to residential areas and intensified Forest Department patrols during dawn hours. They have also called for the intervention of local administrators to secure the required financial support.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab: APEPDCL opens 41 control rooms, keeps 4,056 workers ready to restore power
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: People in Kakinada, East Godavari and Konaseema, the districts likely to bear the brunt, can report power problems on helpline 1912

The Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL) has stepped up its preparedness for Cyclone Arnab and is concentrating on Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Godavari and Kakinada districts, towards which the storm is expected to make landfall.

Following the India Meteorological Department (IMD)’s warning about Cyclone Arnab over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal, the utility has mobilised personnel, machinery and electrical materials to minimise disruptions and speed up power restoration in affected areas.

APEPDCL has opened 30 divisional control rooms, in addition to 11 circle-level control rooms, to monitor the situation and coordinate emergency response. Kakinada and East Godavari have three divisional control rooms each, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema has two.
A separate cell has been established at the corporate office to coordinate manpower deployment round the clock under the supervision of the Chief General Manager (Operations and Customer Service).

APEPDCL CMD I. Prudhvi Tej held a teleconference with senior engineering officials to review cyclone preparedness. The utility has also sought 150 teams of 10 personnel each from the Southern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Limited (APSPDCL) and requested additional materials from it.

The utility has arranged 394 contractor teams comprising 4,056 personnel for emergency response and restoration work. The available resources include 211 diesel generator sets, 273 pole-drilling machines, 517 power saws and 318 earth movers and cranes.

A fleet of 366 departmental and private vehicles has been listed to transport personnel and materials to affected locations. Another 100 mobile handsets have been arranged for communication during emergency operations.

APEPDCL said it had stocks of conductors, cables, distribution transformers and electric poles as of October 25. The inventory includes 425 km of 100 sq. mm AAA conductor, 756 km of 55 sq. mm AAA conductor and 496 km of low-tension aerial-bunched cable. Transformer stocks include 749 single-phase 25 kVA units, 681 three-phase 25 kVA units and 396 three-phase 63 kVA units. These will be used to replace damaged electrical equipment and restore supply.

“We have strengthened our preparedness with control rooms, manpower, machinery and essential materials to respond promptly to cyclone-related disruptions and restore power supply in affected areas,” Mr. Prudhvi Tej told The Hindu.

People can report power supply problems on the helpline 1912. The IMD expects Cyclone Arnab to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of October 28, with winds of 115 to 125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph.

Cyclone Hudhud crossed the coast at Visakhapatnam in October 2014 and damaged 5,727 electric poles and transformers in four north Andhra districts. By the next day it had claimed 21 lives. The power distribution companies deployed over 5,000 employees and hired 1,000 more people to restore supply.

articles.title: Flash floods inundate several areas of Thailand’s Phuket island after heavy rain
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: All three districts of the southern island province, including its capital, Phuket City, were impacted by the flooding

Flash floods on Monday (October 26, 2026) inundated several areas of the island of Phuket in Thailand, one of the country’s major tourist destinations, following heavy rainfall overnight, officials said.
All three districts of the southern island province, including its capital, Phuket City, were impacted by the flooding.

Water levels started to recede by late morning, but some lower-lying areas remained flooded and small vehicles were advised to avoid those areas, according to the provincial deputy governor, Romdon Hayiawae.
He said some parts of the province were also hit with mudslides and officials were working to clear the debris to prevent it from falling into canals and obstructing waterways.

Photos and videos shared on social media show floodwaters flowing into residential areas and filling up several roads, making them impassable. Vehicles are seen partially buried in piles of mud and rocks left behind by the flooding.
About 100 households were affected. There were no reports of casualties, Romdon said.
The Thai Meteorological Department warned of heavy and continuous rain in the southern region until Wednesday (October 28, 2026), which could trigger more flash floods and landslides.

Flooding has battered many parts of Thailand since mid-September, and at least 83 people were reported killed as of Monday (October 26, 2026), according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation.
The Thai capital of Bangkok was inundated in late September after days of torrential rain, forcing thousands to evacuate and causing severe disruptions.

articles.title: Six injured in Russian strikes on Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia, Chernihiv, officials say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Kyiv would halt strikes on Russian oil refineries only if Moscow stopped hitting power infrastructure, or if the U.S. supplied Patriot missiles or allowed Starshield use over Russia
A Russian strike on Ukraine’s south-eastern city of Zaporizhzhia injured four people overnight, regional Governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Telegram on Monday (October 26, 2026).

Two more were injured in Russian strikes on the Chernihiv region, Ukraine’s emergency service said on the messaging app. Also on Telegram, the Russian Defence Ministry said it hit a power station in Ukraine’s second-largest city of Kharkiv, a warehouse in the surrounding region, and another power station in the Khmelnitskiy region. It also said it had targeted port infrastructure in Chornomorsk and a cargo vessel en route to Odesa used for military purposes.

The United States has pressed Ukraine to suspend strikes on Russian oil refineries, which it argues have added to high energy prices, a sensitive issue for the Trump administration amid its war on Iran, as midterm elections approach next month.

In an interview aired on Sunday (October 25, 2026), President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said that for Kyiv to halt the strikes, Moscow must stop hitting power infrastructure. Alternatively, the United States should allow the use of Starshield over Russia to detect missile launch sites, or supply Ukraine with Patriot missiles, he added.

articles.title: Trump says Canada trade deal coming ‘soon’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: President Trump said at a Michigan rally that Canada was “willing to give us anything,” as the White House eased some tariffs following a request from Senator Susan Collins

A trade agreement between the United States and Canada would be reached “pretty soon,” President Donald Trump told a campaign rally on Sunday (October 25, 2026), nine days ahead of crucial U.S. midterm elections.
Tensions between the North American neighbours have been high since trade talks broke down in August 2026, with Mr. Trump imposing a slew of new tariffs in response.

“We’ll have that settled pretty soon. They’re willing to give us anything at this moment,” the President said of an agreement, during the rally in Port Huron, a Michigan town on the U.S.-Canada border hit hard by his tariff war. Mr. Trump once again defended his levies on Canada, and accused it of “ripping off the United States for years.”

The tariffs enforced after the August talks broke down affected about $20 billion worth of goods, ranging from hockey sticks to cement. In response, Canada imposed tolls on an equivalent amount of American products, leading Mr. Trump to retaliate with another round of levies of as much as 50% on certain goods.

The White House removed some of them on Friday (October 23, 2026), in response to a request from Senator Susan Collins, who represents the border State of Maine, which has been disproportionately affected by the trade war. Democrats are targeting Ms. Collins’s seat in their attempt to win control of the Senate from the Republicans, in next Tuesday’s (November 3, 2026) midterms.

Since the start of his second term, Mr. Trump has upended the global trade order by imposing wide-ranging tariffs on friend and foe, saying they had been taking advantage of the United States. He has also explicitly tied some threatened tariffs to political or foreign policy objectives.

articles.title: Why did Tinder’s scam detection fail, and what should Indian users do?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: U.S. lawmakers shared troubling statistics about how dating app users on Tinder and Hinge were matching with scammers, due to outdated AI protections
Earlier in October, U.S. lawmakers revealed how users of dating apps were being exposed to serious financial and physical risks. They pinned this to the outdated AI stack in these applications.

In an investigation centred around the Match Group, the lawmakers found that the algorithm matched U.S. users of dating apps like Tinder and Hinge with scammers. The report, titled ‘Outmatched: Tinder, Scammers, and Match Group’s Efforts to Catch Up’, highlighted that users connected with nearly 1.5 million scammers on these two popular dating applications in the first nine months of 2025.
At the core of these disturbing findings were outdated machine learning models installed to detect bad actors. These hadn’t been updated in years, per the report.

This information came from internal documents that the Match Group shared with the committee, led by senator Maggie Hassan. As the accuracy of scam detection dropped, Tinder began depending on other measures that it knew were often ineffective.
“In fact, Match Group knew that Tinder was more likely to show a profile if it belonged to a scammer or other bad actor rather than a regular user,” stated an official press release about the report.
However, the investigation acknowledged that the Match Group later put in place new safety measures, such as an AI model in Tinder this year that was designed to detect scammers and bad actors.

The report included statements from victims who described how romance scammers cheated them out of tens of thousands of dollars after building a relationship with them on the dating apps. A common trend was to cite a major emergency in order to pressure the victim into sending over money. Using the victims’ phone number and/or email ID, the scammers would proceed to harass them online until the victim sometimes paid them in the hopes of de-escalating their aggression.
Another type of scam involved the same malicious user operating as different people on the same dating app, to ensnare more victims.

The report pointed to an inconsistent dating app AI strategy, where patchy machine learning systems led to heavy caseloads and “overwhelmed” human moderators who were unable to focus on visibly risky accounts. Per a document from the Match Group itself, Tinder could have better tackled dangerous accounts by building better AI signals or reducing its reliance on manual rules.

“In practice, these moderation lapses meant that bad actors that reached moderation were not immediately banned and instead may have continued to interact with and harm legitimate users until the platform gathered additional evidence,” explained the report.

A bouquet of dating apps come under the Match Group, including Tinder, Hinge, Match (formerly Match.com), Plenty of Fish, and more such offerings catering to users in diverse countries and cultural communities.

In other words, a security lapse in one app comes with serious implications for the users of other Match Group-owned apps. Tinder and Hinge are popular in India as well, claiming the top ranks in terms of downloads via app marketplaces.

articles.title: Jordanian security forces arrest 3 men for deadly attack on church
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Public Security Directorate said the three suspects were arrested following a dawn shootout and that all three were wounded
Jordanian security forces arrested three men on Monday (October 26, 2026) for an attack on a Greek Orthodox Church that killed nine people and wounded more than two dozen.
The Public Security Directorate said the three suspects were arrested following a dawn shootout and that all three were wounded.
No members of the security forces were injured in the dawn operation in Karak, south of Jordan's capital, Amman. Karak is home to a minority Christian population.
The attack on the Greek Orthodox Church in Karak took place on Friday (October 23, 2026) during a funeral. Three men were reported to have taken part in the attack.
There was still no claim of responsibility, and no armed group has been accused of the attack.
Jordan's Interior Minister Mazen Al-Faraya identified the three men as those responsible for the attack.
“The security services have fulfilled their duties, resulting in the capture of those who carried out this terrorist act,” he said in a phone interview with state TV Al-Mamlaka .
“They put up fierce resistance against the security forces, but were ultimately subdued and taken into custody, having sustained severe injuries.”

He added that there “are three individuals involved; they were identified early on in the wake of the terrorist incident, and the security services employed all the means at their disposal to apprehend them”.
King Abdullah II directed authorities to respond with “an iron fist” against what he called the outlaws of Islam and anyone attempting to undermine the unity of the Jordanian people.

articles.title: What was leaked in the Censor Board data breach? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Hindu reported over the weekend that entire application forms to the censor board by filmmakers, including commercially sensitive distribution agreements, were lying exposed on the Internet Archive

The story so far: A data breach at the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) left hundreds of applications’ data exposed online, The Hindu found. The data comes from over 500 titles, of which dozens are feature films. The leak comes from the censor board’s e-Cinepramaan portal, used by filmmakers to submit their applications. The records ranged from December 2025 to August 2026.

The leaked documents included shooting scripts, with detailed shot-by-shot translations and other annotations. These scripts appear to have been specifically prepared for the censor board’s review of these films — one script even included labels on swear words used over the course of the film and other clarifications on dialogue.

The breached data also included a summary of cuts that were ordered by the CBFC. This is supposed to be public information anyway under Section 5A(2) of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, but the censor board put this data behind an “under maintenance” message on its website .

In what could be the most sensitive of the exposed documents, film distribution agreements — both from international filmmakers distributing into India and Indian filmmakers authorising dubbed versions in a different part of the country — were exposed. At least three such agreements had unredacted or improperly redacted information on what fees were paid to license a film for distribution in India. The Hindu is withholding specifics here.

“Commercial agreements in the film industry often contain carefully negotiated provisions governing creative control, casting, remuneration, profit-sharing, intellectual property rights, promotional obligations, and even specific conditions concerning a film’s storyline, portrayal or production,” Vasundhara S., managing partner at Verum Legal told The Hindu .

“When commercially sensitive or specially negotiated creative terms enter the public domain, the confidentiality underpinning these agreements is compromised,” Ms. Vasundhara said. “Such disclosures can weaken negotiating positions, reveal commercially valuable information, influence future contractual negotiations and potentially expose parties to disputes arising from confidentiality obligations.”

“If I am a competing party or a counterparty, I’d be in a much better position to negotiate now that I have confirmation as to what terms these guys would agree to for certain types of works, beyond what is generally known in the market,” Abhinav Hansaraman, a commercial lawyer in Delhi said.

The documents were posted as dockets that contained practically everything but a copy of the film itself, and posted on the site of the non-profit Internet Archive portal. The data dump, most of it was posted on a single day, lay on the site for days, open to anyone to review and download. It is unclear if the data dump’s existence was known to anyone.

The majority of the documents were posted earlier this month, but were all taken down on October 12. The user, whose display ID was former CBFC chairman Prasoon Joshi’s name in Russian, also deleted their account. The Hindu was unable to contact them.

Last week, The Hindu contacted the CBFC for comment on the breach. The censor board did not appear to have immediate information on the breach. A week after being provided granular details of what documents were leaked from which film application, CBFC chairperson Shashi Shekhar Vempati said in a statement that it was looking into the breach. “CBFC has reviewed the information shared regarding alleged unauthorised access to CBFC’s eCinePramaan Portal,” the CBFC said. “However, based on the information examined so far, no trace has been found of the certification-related documents that were claimed to have been accessed.”

The Internet Archive told The Hindu in a statement that the account in question was taken down by the user themselves. “As a matter of caution, a complaint has been filed with Cybercrime, and CERT-In has also been notified of the allegations and provided with the information shared,” the CBFC added in its statement to The Hindu . CERT-in is India’s computer emergency response team, which is tasked with handling data breach and hacking incidents.

“The technical team has also conducted a thorough analysis of the servers and databases to assess whether any external attacks may have compromised their security,” CBFC added. “The findings of this analysis are being considered alongside the ongoing forensic examination.”

articles.title: Nedumbassery luxury car crash: Audio clip of an accused describing incident emerges as possible key evidence
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ernakulam Additional District Court reserves verdict in bail pleas for October 28

The Ernakulam Rural Police investigating the Nedumbassery luxury car crash that killed three persons claim to have secured an audio clip reportedly sent by one of the four accused to his friends, describing in detail the tragic turn of events shortly after the accident.

It was one of the digital pieces of evidence the police produced before the Ernakulam Additional District Court to oppose the bail applications of the accused on Monday (October 26, 2026). While the prosecution opposed the bail pleas, citing the need for police custody of the accused for more detailed interrogation, the defence countered that there was no requirement for further police custody and that the abetment charges against accused Nos. 2 to 4 would not stand.

The Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Angamaly, on October 17, had rejected the bail applications of all four accused. The Nedumbassery police had arrested four 19-year-olds – Suhail Sajeev, who allegedly drove the car under the influence of alcohol, and three co-passengers, Ninav, Ameen Sha, and Joyal S.

According to the police, Joyal, who had fled the scene immediately after the incident, sent an audio clip to one of his friends describing the incident in detail. “In the clip, he says that Suhail was heavily drunk and was driving at a very high speed when he knocked down three youths travelling on a scooter. He also claims that Suhail called his father immediately after the incident. He even shared news links related to the accident,” police sources said.

Meanwhile, the police are still tracing witnesses to the incident. Investigators claim to have tracked down a key eyewitness, an online cab driver, after extensively examining CCTV footage. “He was parked near the accident site and was checking his mobile phone. On hearing the sound of the collision, he rushed to the scene. Likewise, we are trying to trace more witnesses, which is proving to be a difficult task,” police sources said.
While Suhail and Ninav were taken into custody from the spot immediately after the accident, Ameen and Joyal, who fled the scene, were apprehended in Alappuzha the following day.
The accident occurred on October 11 around 1.45 a.m., killing Devika, 21, Gopika, 22, and Ijaz, 21.

Suhail allegedly visited three bars in the hours leading up to the incident and was driving at a speed of around 165 kmph at the time of the crash. His blood alcohol content, reportedly, was five times more than the permissible limits, the police had said.
The Excise Department subsequently suspended the licences of all three bars on charges of serving alcohol to an underage person.
The incident attracted considerable media attention, and the Opposition LDF raised the matter in the Assembly. Controversy also erupted over Suhail being sent to a Borstal school instead of a prison.

While rejecting the bail applications, the Magistrate of the Angamaly court noted that there was every possibility of the accused attempting to influence or intimidate witnesses and tamper with evidence.

“It was also pointed out by the counsel for the father of one of the deceased that accused no. 1 shouted that his father would take care of everything. According to the prosecution, the said circumstance, considered along with the nature of the occurrence and the fact that material witnesses are yet to be examined, gives rise to an apprehension that the accused may attempt to influence witnesses or interfere with the remaining investigation,” the order said.

articles.title: Fatal luxury car crash: Keralam judge booked under MV Act as registered owner of vehicle driven by minor son
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Section 199A of Motor Vehicles Act stipulates that where an offence has been committed by a juvenile, the guardian or the owner of the motor vehicle shall be deemed guilty and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly

The Kochi City police on Monday (October 26, 2026) arraigned as an accused an Additional District Judge who is the father of the 17-year-old boy accused of causing the death of a man after allegedly ramming his luxury car into the victim’s scooter at Cheranalloor in Keralam in the early hours of Sunday.

The judge, who is posted in a court in Irinjalakkuda in Thrissur district, has been booked under Section 199A of the Motor Vehicles Act, which stipulates that where an offence has been committed by a juvenile, the guardian of the juvenile or the owner of the motor vehicle shall be deemed guilty of the contravention and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. He is the registered owner of the car involved in the accident.

“Steps are now being taken in compliance with the Supreme Court guidelines that apply when a judge is booked. We will have to intimate the district judiciary and the High Court,” S. Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar, District Police Chief (Kochi City), told The Hindu .

The victim’s family, along with various political and youth outfits, had been clamouring for a case to be registered against the judge. In the early hours of Monday, the Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) granted bail to the teenager citing the absence of any previous criminal antecedents.

The deceased was identified as Jayabalakrishnan, 55, of Chittur, Cheranalloor. He was returning after closing his eatery at Chittur when the accident happened and succumbed to his injuries on the spot. The accident occurred around 2.20 a.m. at Maraparambu on Container Road in Cheranalloor.
According to the FIR, the teenager was travelling alone in the car from Vallarpadam towards Kalamassery when it hit the scooter, which was moving in the same direction.

The boy was initially released on bail from the police station under Section 8 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015. A case was registered against the minor under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), dealing with rash driving and causing death by a rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide. Later in the day, the police added Section 105 of the BNS, which prescribes punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder, to the FIR. The section was added amid protests and criticism against the police for releasing the accused on station bail.

articles.title: Copious rain triggers seven new landslips in Nilgiris
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two men and a woman suffered injuries in rain-related mishaps. District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru said four relief camps have been set up.

Persistent downpours over the hill district of The Nilgiris triggered seven new landslips and uprooted 15 trees in the 24-hour period ending at 7 a.m. on Monday (October 26, 2026), further disrupting normal life and road connectivity at some places.

According to rainfall data released by the district administration, the district recorded a total rainfall of 734.5 mm and average rainfall of 23.69 mm. Severe weather conditions battered several places. Kinnakorai in Kundah taluk (110 mm) and Kotagiri (68 mm) received heavy rain. A total of 14 rain gauge stations, including Burliar (59 mm), Yedappalli (54 mm) and Kodanadu (42 mm) recorded moderate rain. Two men and a woman suffered injuries in rain-related mishaps, including tree fall, and three huts were partially damaged.
The Nilgiris had recorded 62 landslips when the district received a cumulative total rainfall of 453.9 mm in the previous 24-hour period that ended on Sunday (October 25, 2026) morning.
District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru announced holiday for all schools in Udhagamandalam, Coonoor, Kotagiri and Kundah taluks in the Nilgiris on Monday (October 26) owing to rain.

Ms. Thanneeru said four relief camps have been set up in schools and community halls to accommodate people, who get affected by rain, tree fall or landslip. A total of 65 people including tribals from three-four hamlets near Burliyar and Katteri were shifted to the relief camp set up at St. Antony’s Higher Secondary School, Coonoor, on Sunday (October 25) evening as the region had witnessed lightning strikes.

Ms. Tanneeru said they were shifted to the relief camp as a precautionary measure. They will stay at the camps for the next few days. Some of them went to their hamlets to feed cattle and domestic animals on Monday morning.
According to the Collector, officials from the National Highways Department and geotechnical experts were assessing the damages caused by landslips on Mettupalayam-Udhagamandalam Road on Monday.

The traffic between Nilgiris and Coimbatore is currently being diverted via Kotagiri as a portion of the road washed away near Burliyar in Coimbatore district limits on the Mettupalayam-Udhagamandalam Road that passes via Coonoor. “Vehicular traffic through the road can be allowed only after stabilising the damage” she added.

articles.title: IIIT Hyderabad Junction road closure extended for another three months from October 27
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Cyberabad Traffic Police says traffic construction of multi-level flyover and associated works could continue for at least a year

The road between DLF Gate No. 1 and Gachibowli Traffic Police Station will remain closed for another three months from Tuesday (October 27, 2026) to facilitate construction of a multi-level flyover and underpass at IIIT Junction, the Cyberabad Traffic Police said.

The closure, which was initially imposed for 90 days from July 1, has been extended to facilitate faster execution of the construction work. The stretch will be opened partially in phases depending on the progress of the works and availability of road space, police said.

As per the revised traffic advisory issued on Monday (October 26, 2026), vehicles travelling from Radisson Hotel towards IIIT Junction will be allowed up to DLF Gate No. 1 and stopped beyond the gate. Commuters will have to take the Gachibowli Junction route, turn right towards Indiranagar and proceed towards IIIT Junction.
TCS employees using the Non-SEZ (CMC) gate will continue to use their existing entry and exit point.
Traffic travelling from Lingampally towards DLF Road will be diverted at Gachibowli Traffic Police Station and routed via IIIT Junction, Gachibowli Junction and Radisson Junction before reaching DLF.
The traffic police said construction of the flyover and associated works could continue for at least a year and warned of congestion around IIIT Junction during the construction period.

Regular commuters, particularly IT employees, were advised to plan their journeys and use alternative routes. The Cyberabad Traffic Police also appealed to motorists to cooperate with traffic personnel to ensure smooth movement.

articles.title: Maharashtra CM responds positively to Telangana’s request for 152-metre Tummidihatti barrage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Joint committee of officials to examine technical feasibility, submergence and compensation issues

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has responded positively to Telangana’s request to increase the height of the proposed Tummidihatti barrage across the Pranahita river from 148 metres to 152 metres, while making it clear that the project should not adversely affect Maharashtra or its people.

At a meeting with Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy in Mumbai on Monday (October 6, 2026), Mr. Fadnavis proposed constituting a joint committee headed by the Principal Secretaries of the Irrigation Departments of the two States to examine the technical feasibility of the proposal, water availability, submergence implications and other related issues.

The committee will assess the likely impact on agricultural land and local communities, compensation requirements and possible alternatives before preparing a timeline and roadmap for further action. The Central Water Commission (CWC) will continue its technical examination within its jurisdiction.

Telangana Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy made a detailed presentation explaining why a barrage at 152 metres would be more viable than the 148-metre height envisaged in the 2016 agreement. He cited the need to maximise gravity-based water conveyance in view of rising power costs, energy requirements, environmental concerns, climate change and long-term operational sustainability.

Mr. Uttam Kumar Reddy also conveyed the Telangana Government’s willingness to compensate farmers in Maharashtra whose agricultural land might be affected by submergence, in accordance with that State’s land acquisition guidelines and compensation policies.

Chief Miniter Revanth Reddy highlighted the long-standing demand for irrigation and drinking water facilities in the tribal-dominated and economically backward Adilabad region. He said the project was important not merely as an irrigation initiative but also as an instrument for the social and economic transformation of communities that had remained deprived of development opportunities for decades.

Recalling the historic ‘ Jal, Jangal, Zameen’ struggle led by tribal leader Kumram Bheem , the Chief Minister emphasised the aspirations of Adivasi communities for access to water and improved livelihoods. He pointed out that efforts to provide irrigation to the region had been continuing since October 6, 1975, but the aspirations of its people had remained largely unfulfilled despite several initiatives over five decades.

The Chief Minister also underlined the historical and cultural ties between Telangana and Maharashtra, including their shared heritage associated with the erstwhile Hyderabad State. He said cooperation on the barrage would strengthen relations between the two States and contribute to the development of backward regions on both sides of the border.

Referring to the proposed defence and civilian airport facilities at Adilabad, he said the infrastructure could act as a catalyst for development in the region and adjoining areas of Maharashtra. The barrage, he added, could also strengthen connectivity and economic cooperation between communities along the inter-State border.

Responding to the Telangana delegation, Mr. Fadnavis acknowledged the developmental needs of the region and expressed willingness to reconsider the request, subject to the completion of the necessary technical, environmental and administrative assessments.

According to Telangana Chief Minister’s Office, Mr. Fadnavis had no hesitation in supporting Telangana’s water requirements if the project did not adversely affect Maharashtra or its people. He stressed the need to resolve the issue through mutual consultations, in a spirit of friendship, brotherhood and good-neighbourly relations.

The proposed joint committee is expected to bring together officials and technical experts from both States to examine the competing requirements and concerns and work out a mutually acceptable way forward.

articles.title: Marine Le Pen, France’s far-right candidate, launches presidential bid
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Vowing to “restore the rule of law”, Marine Le Pen said French nationality will once again become a privilege that is either inherited or earned
Marine Le Pen, France's far-right candidate to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, kicked off her campaign on Sunday (October 25, 2026) vowing to "restore the rule of law" if elected next year.

Ms. Le Pen, the frontrunner in the polls, seems to be benefiting from the convulsions France has been going through for weeks, which has seen violence flare on the side-lines of mass cost-of-living rallies.
"We are going to restore the rule of law," she said, after looting and arson erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations last weekend.

She was addressing 8,500 supporters of her nationalist, anti-immigration party in the city of Orleans, where Joan of Arc, revered by the far right as a symbol of national resistance, lifted an English siege in 1429.
"We are proposing for the country not a return to the past, but the dawn of a new era," the 58-year-old told the crowd, which broke into chants of "We're going to win, we're going to win."
Ms. Le Pen vowed to preserve France's cultural identity, from its language and traditions to its values and way of life, drawing thunderous cheers from supporters waving French flags.
Supporter Charlene Malingre, wearing a scarf emblazoned with the words "Marine President", said she was increasingly concerned about insecurity in France.
"I think Marine Le Pen could save France from the state it's in today, particularly when it comes to the economy, security and maintaining law and order," the 23-year-old told AFP.

More than 4,00,000 people marched in major French cities on Saturday (October 24, 2026) to protest against the rising cost of living. Clashes erupted after groups of masked protesters broke away from the demonstrations.
Police made more than 1,300 arrests and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez blamed much of the violence on "ultra-left" extremists.
Similar nationwide protests a week earlier also descended into unrest, following four weeks of student demonstrations over the poor state of France's schools.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu will hold talks with high school student organisations on Monday (October 26, 2026), a leader of one of the groups told AFP.

articles.title: Iran says officials from Saudi, Turkiye, Pakistan to visit Tehran for security talks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The meeting was proposed during a visit by Pakistani Army chief Asim Munir to Tehran last week, says Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary of Iran’s SNSC

An Iranian official said on Monday (October 26, 2026) that senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan will visit Tehran for talks over regional security, without specifying when the meeting would take place.

"As agreed, Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani Army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish Intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin will participate in this meeting," said Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council (SNSC).
He said the meeting will be held with Iran's Security chief Mohsen Rezaei.

"This four-party meeting in Tehran could represent an important and effective step towards building lasting regional security, and we hope this initiative will contribute to establishing a stable region," said Mr. Kani in an interview with state television, without elaborating.
He did not specify when the meeting would take place but said it was proposed during a visit by Pakistani Army chief Asim Munir to Tehran last week .

War has engulfed West Asia since February when the United States and Israel launched a wave of surprise attacks on Iran, while Washington and Tehran were in the midst of negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme.

An April ceasefire brought an end to the initial phase of intense bombardment but the two sides have continued to vie for control over the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel.

articles.title: AI’s costs fall unevenly across workers; IIT Madras paper flags surveillance, work stress
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Whitepaper highlights risks to entry-level career paths and gaps in evidence on job quality and informal employment

The costs of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption fall unevenly across workers, with entry-level jobs particularly at risk, according to a whitepaper by the Centre for Responsible AI (CeRAI) at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT-Madras).

“The entry-level career pipeline is especially at risk,” the paper says, highlighting differences in how AI affects entry-level and experienced workers, formal and informal workers, urban and rural workers, and employees in micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and large firms.

Titled ‘How AI Is Reconfiguring Work in India: A Task-Based Framework for Understanding Augmentation, Displacement, New Roles and the Changing Structure of Jobs’, the paper examines how AI automates tasks within jobs and how this can lead to changes in work, new roles or displacement.

The paper identifies differences in firms’ ability to adopt AI. Large companies can absorb the fixed costs of integrating and customising advanced models, while MSMEs depend more on narrow, subsidised tools. It also flags differences between English and regional-language work, noting that Indian-language AI performs less well on nuanced, code-switched conversations.

Automation is also creating new roles, including robot operators and AI escalation specialists. However, the paper says its evidence does not systematically track whether such roles offer stable employment or piecework, a distinction that affects how much of the productivity gains reaches workers.

The paper says its framework is “largely silent” on changes in job quality because Indian evidence is limited. It identifies wages, workplace monitoring, work intensity, stress and burnout, career progression, the quality of human interaction and responsibility for errors as areas requiring further study.

Among the questions it raises is whether AI will bring new forms of performance tracking, such as scoring the calls handled by BPO employees after AI has taken over routine queries, or using dashboards to track productivity among MSME shop-floor workers.

It also asks whether AI could leave workers handling a more demanding stream of exceptions after automating less-intensive tasks. The authors caution that the available Indian sources do not systematically measure these dimensions.

Junior roles have traditionally served as apprenticeships, with routine tasks helping workers develop the judgement needed for senior positions, the paper says. If AI automates tasks such as password resets, basic contract reviews and boilerplate coding, it raises questions about how new employees will acquire that experience.
The issue is particularly relevant to India’s IT, business process outsourcing (BPO), finance and professional-services sectors, which have historically hired large numbers of entry-level graduates.

One possible response is to redesign junior roles around supervising and correcting AI rather than performing routine tasks. But the paper says it remains an open question whether firms will redesign career paths or simply hire fewer junior employees.

The paper notes that its framework relies largely on formal-sector evidence, despite informal work accounting for a substantially larger share of India’s workforce than the formal jobs examined in detail.

articles.title: Amid row, Keralam’s UDF govt says cost of generic SMA drug can be cut further
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Health Minister K. Muraleedharan tells Assembly that UDF government’s aim, eventually, is to offer medicines free of cost to all SMA patients. LDF Opposition stages walkout after adjournment motion rejected

The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Keralam on Monday strongly defended the switch to a generic drug for patients with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and said it would try to further reduce the price of the drug.

Speaking in the State Legislative Assembly, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan announced that the UDF government’s aim, eventually, was to offer medicines free of cost to all SMA patients. The matter will be discussed with Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and an announcement will be made in due course, Mr. Muraleedharan said.

The Health Minister was responding to an adjournment motion moved by the CPI(M)-led Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) with regard to the controversy over the generic SMA drug and the unconnected development where the government had formed a 16-member task force with the aim of establishing a ‘Kerala Holistic Model for Health, Wellness and Longevity.’

While the Opposition accused the government of launching ‘clinical trials’ on SMA patients and pushing a corporatisation agenda in the health sector through the task force, Chief Minister Mr. Satheesan said both decisions were taken in the best interests of the people.
The Assembly witnessed a sharp confrontation between the ruling and Opposition fronts over the two issues, leading to a walkout by the latter after the adjournment motion was rejected.
With regard to the generic SMA drug, Mr. Satheesan said the government decision gave patients access to a generic drug that cost just ₹15,000 when the branded version cost ₹6.5 lakh for 12 days.

The generic alternative, marketed by Natco Pharma, had the support of court orders and statutory clearances from government agencies concerned, he said. “It has brought immense relief to the families of the patients. Our belief is that the price can be reduced further, to ₹9,000,” Mr. Satheesan said. He also congratulated Mr. Muraleedharan and the Health Department for taking the decision.

However, Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan said the government was “misleading everyone” by depicting the LDF as being opposed to generic drugs and that it favoured the costly Risdiplam, marketed by Roche Pharmaceuticals. Mr. Vijayan said the LDF has always encouraged generic medicines. “But here, the issue pertained to clinical trials of the SMA drug,” he said.
The LDF also targeted the composition of the task force; specifically the inclusion of Deepak Singhal, a former Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary.

Mr. Vijayan said that Mr. Singhal’s links to Global Trade and Technology Council (India) (GTTCI Healthcare Ventures) was “a matter of concern.” Corporates viewed the health sector as a milch cow and his presence on the task force illustrated the UDF’s “corporatisation agenda” for the sector, he said.

The Chief Minister, however, swept aside the charge, stating that the 16-member task force was composed of "knowledge partners.” Its aim was to devise strategies to reduce healthcare costs and ensure early detection of diseases and their prevention. This was important at a time when investment giants such as Blackstone have entered the State’s health sector and medical bills in private hospitals were soaring, making such institutions inaccessible to the general public, he said.

Earlier, K. Premkumar of the CPI(M), K. Rajan of the CPI, and P.K. Praveen of the RJD had moved the adjournment motion. They sought a discussion in the House on the perils faced by the State’s health sector arising from the government decisions to include representatives of “private hospitals, laboratories and pharma companies” in the task force and the concerns over clinical trials related to the SMA drug.

articles.title: Seven caveats in the claim about turning mercury into gold with nuclear fusion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: In a preprint paper uploaded to the arXiv repository in July 2025, Marathon scientists had predicted this process could produce roughly 2 tonnes of gold annually for every gigawatt (GW) of thermal fusion power

A San Francisco-based company named Marathon Fusion announced on October 21 that it had ‘converted’ mercury into gold in an experiment in September and that it had achieved a production rate tenfold greater than a record reported by CERN in 2025.

The company has also proposed a programme in which mercury-198 is exposed to high-energy neutrons produced by nuclear fusion — in an existing power plant — converting it into radioactive mercury-197, which subsequently decays into stable gold-197. In a preprint paper uploaded to the arXiv repository in July 2025, Marathon scientists had predicted this process could produce roughly 2 tonnes of gold annually for every gigawatt (GW) of thermal fusion power.

This said, the company has not said if its recent claim has been independently verified — there are no public records indicating that — nor has it disclosed how much gold it actually produced. Overall, there are at least seven caveats around the claims and the hype that has erupted around it.

In nuclear fusion, light nuclei, such as deuterium and tritium, are forced together, releasing high-energy neutrons and energy. The proposal is to have these neutrons strike mercury nuclei and eventually produce gold nuclei. The latter is called nuclear transmutation, not nuclear fusion. Neither the gold nor the mercury nuclei undergo any fusion of their own. Nuclear transmutation is well-known in nuclear physics. In other words the claim about “using” fusion to turn mercury into gold can be misleading.

On its website, Marathon Fusion has published data showing the energy signatures associated with mercury-197 and its decay into gold-197. It is not possible to infer how much gold was produced from this information, nor its purity or how efficiently the process works. Marathon has also not placed a detailed experimental methodology or independent verification in the public domain. Its prior research, described in the preprint paper, was based on computer simulations.

In 2025, CERN had reported that interactions between lead ions at the Large Hadron Collider had produced around 86 billion gold nuclei from 2015 to 2018. This is just around 0.029 billionths of gram — about the amount of gold you can buy with 0.0000414 paise. These nuclei existed for mere fractions of a second before disintegrating further. CERN was also just conducting particle-physics research, not attempting to manufacture gold on a commercial scale. And Marathon Fusion has not explained exactly how it calculated its tenfold improvement.

In the 2025 preprint paper, the authors estimated that a suitable nuclear fusion plant could produce around 2,000 kg of gold every year per gigawatt of thermal power. The figure is rooted in certain advanced computer simulations of neutron transport and nuclear reactions. It is not based on the workings of a functional, commercial reactor. Marathon Fusion has also described plans for a reactor with a fusion power target of just 1 kW, which is one-million-times smaller than 1 GW. Long story short, even if Marathon Fusion’s claimed experiment in September demonstrated converting mercury to gold, it cannot be used to validate the company’s projections of producing gold on an industrial scale.

Only around 10% of the mercury that occurs naturally is mercury-198, which is the isotope Marathon Fusion proposes to use. However, its computer simulations assumed mercury enriched to 90% mercury-198. This will require a programme to enrich mercury isotopes on an industrial scale. Second, mercury is extremely toxic, so the facilities will have to have specialised containment materials and protocols and environmental safeguards. Marathon Fusion has acknowledged these difficulties and has proposed technological solutions but their practicality and costs have yet to be determined at scale.

The Marathon Fusion way to make gold is not implausible but the resulting gold will be radioactive. Other nuclear reactions happening at the same time will also create other radioactive isotopes, including gold-195, which has a half-life of around 186 days. And according to Marathon’s own simulations, the resulting gold mix will need around 6.8 years to meet one low-level radioactive waste threshold, 13.7 years to fall below a specified radioactive material labelling threshold, and 17.7 years to meet a more conservative benchmark. It will be possible to purify the isotopes to reduce these timelines but not without adding to the costs.

The Marathon Fusion website says producing gold in this way could roughly double the revenue of fusion power plants without compromising electricity output. To this end, the preprint paper modelled a 1.5-GW thermal fusion power plant that cost $3 billion to build and which operates at 100% capacity for three decades while converting 40% of its thermal output to electricity. In this scenario the plant will generate around $263 million a year from electricity sold at $50 per megawatt-hour. And producing three tonnes of gold a year and selling it at $100,000 per kilogram would add $300 million in revenue. The problem? Commercial fusion power does not yet exist and these figures are all based on expectations of the future.

In the 2025 preprint paper, the authors estimated that a suitable nuclear fusion plant could produce around 2,000 kg of gold every year per gigawatt of thermal power. The figure is rooted in certain advanced computer simulations of neutron transport and nuclear reactions. It is not based on the workings of a functional, commercial reactor. Marathon Fusion has also described plans for a reactor with a fusion power target of just 1 kW, which is one-million-times smaller than 1 GW. Long story short, even if Marathon Fusion’s claimed experiment in September demonstrated converting mercury to gold, it cannot be used to validate the company’s projections of producing gold on an industrial scale.

Only around 10% of the mercury that occurs naturally is mercury-198, which is the isotope Marathon Fusion proposes to use. However, its computer simulations assumed mercury enriched to 90% mercury-198. This will require a programme to enrich mercury isotopes on an industrial scale. Second, mercury is extremely toxic, so the facilities will have to have specialised containment materials and protocols and environmental safeguards. Marathon Fusion has acknowledged these difficulties and has proposed technological solutions but their practicality and costs have yet to be determined at scale.

The Marathon Fusion way to make gold is not implausible but the resulting gold will be radioactive. Other nuclear reactions happening at the same time will also create other radioactive isotopes, including gold-195, which has a half-life of around 186 days. And according to Marathon’s own simulations, the resulting gold mix will need around 6.8 years to meet one low-level radioactive waste threshold, 13.7 years to fall below a specified radioactive material labelling threshold, and 17.7 years to meet a more conservative benchmark. It will be possible to purify the isotopes to reduce these timelines but not without adding to the costs.

The Marathon Fusion website says producing gold in this way could roughly double the revenue of fusion power plants without compromising electricity output. To this end, the preprint paper modelled a 1.5-GW thermal fusion power plant that cost $3 billion to build and which operates at 100% capacity for three decades while converting 40% of its thermal output to electricity. In this scenario the plant will generate around $263 million a year from electricity sold at $50 per megawatt-hour. And producing three tonnes of gold a year and selling it at $100,000 per kilogram would add $300 million in revenue. The problem? Commercial fusion power does not yet exist and these figures are all based on expectations of the future.
